n: Seasons occur because Earth revolves around the Sun and has an axial tilt of 23½°. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 19-27]
Earth’s rotation causes day and night, not seasons. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 19-27]

Earth’s revolution needs axial tilt to produce seasons. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 19-27]
Distance from the Sun has only a minor or slight role in producing seasons. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 19-27]
Earth’s revolution combined with axial tilt causes seasons. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 19-27]

1.x: Cities near the Tropic of Cancer: Ranchi (Jharkhand), Agartala (Tripura), Aizawl (Mizoram), and Ujjain and Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh).

Consider the following statements:

2. The Tropic of Cancer passes through Iran.
3. The Equator passes through Indonesia.
4. At 1° interval, 179 parallels and 360 meridians are drawn on the globe.
How many of the above statements are correct?
1.x: Statement 2 is wrong: the Tropic of Cancer crosses 17 countries (Mexico, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Oman, India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, China …) but not Iran. The Equator passes Kenya, Colombia and Indonesia; the globe has 179 parallels and 360 meridians at 1°.

1.s: Why 1 second is added to the clocks i.e UTC (Coordinated Universal Time) on December, 2016 just before midnight?
o: Due to slowing of earth's rotation
Due to quickening of earth's rotation
1.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
1.x: A leap second was added to UTC at the end of 31 December 2016 because the Earth's rotation is gradually slowing, so atomic time runs ahead of solar time.

I. Cuba
II. Greece
III. Iraq
IV. Costa Rica
V. Japan Which one of the following sequential orders gives the correct arrangement of the countries according to their standard time from ahead to behind GMT?
1.x: Japan (+9), Iraq (+3) and Greece (+2) are ahead of GMT; Cuba (−5) and Costa Rica (−6) are behind: V, III, II, I, IV.

1.x: Counting overseas territories, the UK (9), Australia (9), Denmark (5) and New Zealand (5) have more than four time zones; Brazil has exactly four – so only four.

1.x: London, Lisbon and Accra all keep GMT; Addis Ababa (Ethiopia, ~38°45'E) keeps UTC+3, so its clock time differs.

1.s:
Consider the following statements:

2. UTC is based only on solar observation.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
1.x: GMT is mean solar time at Greenwich; UTC is maintained by atomic caesium clocks and adjusted with leap seconds, so statement 2 is wrong.
xa: The **Prime Meridian (0°)** runs through the **Royal Observatory, Greenwich**, adopted in **1884**.
⚠ UTC = **caesium** clocks; **NavIC** = **rubidium** clocks.
**IST = GMT + 5 h 30 min** (APPSC **2019**).

1.s: The Prime Meridian, the reference for Greenwich Mean Time, was adopted at the International Meridian Conference in which year?
1.x: The Prime Meridian through the Royal Observatory, Greenwich was adopted at the International Meridian Conference of 1884. 1851 is the year of Foucault's pendulum, 1947 the year a single IST was adopted, and 1569 the year of the Mercator projection.
xs: The Prime Meridian was adopted at the **International Meridian Conference, 1884** — option **(2)**.
**1947** is when a single **IST** was adopted after Independence.
Separate **Bombay and Calcutta times** also date **from 1884**.
xa: The Prime Meridian runs through the **Royal Observatory, Greenwich**.
**GMT** = mean solar time at Greenwich.
**UTC** is kept by **atomic (caesium) clocks**.

1.s: Which natural unit of time is based on the Moon's revolution?
1.x: The month comes from the Moon's revolution; the day from rotation and the year from the Earth's revolution.

1.s:
Consider the following statements about Daylight Saving Time:
1. Clocks are advanced by one hour in summer to use evening light.
2. India follows Daylight Saving Time.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
1.x: Under DST clocks go forward one hour in summer at mid and high latitudes; India does not use it.

1.s: Which of the following cities has the same clock time as Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai?
1.x: Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai and Colombo observe UTC+5:30. Nepal uses UTC+5:45 and therefore does not have the same clock time.
1.tq: Start with the sure UTC+5:30 pair and distinguish it from nearby quarter-hour offsets.
xs: **Colombo** shares IST's clock time (**UTC+5:30**) with Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai — option **(2)**.
**Nepal** (Kathmandu) uses **UTC+5:45**, so it differs.
xa: **IST = GMT + 5 h 30 min**, based on **82°30'E**.
India **does not use DST**.
Kiribati's Line Islands (**UTC+14**) are first to see a new day.

1.s: Which one of the following countries uses a single time zone despite its considerable east-west extent?
1.x: China uses one official time zone throughout the country despite its large longitudinal span.
1.tq: Use the exception to the expected relationship between longitudinal width and number of time zones.
xs: **China** uses **one zone despite its width** — option **(2)**.
**Russia** has **11** zones; **France** **12** (with overseas territories).
xa: India too uses a single IST; the north-east-vs-west gap is ~**2 hours**.
Theoretical division: **24 zones** of **15°**.

1.s: Theoretically, the world is divided into how many time zones of 15° each?
1.x: 360° ÷ 15° gives 24 theoretical time zones; in practice there are more because of half- and quarter-hour offsets.

1.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) is kept by caesium atomic clocks.
2. NavIC, a constellation of 7 satellites, times its signals with caesium atomic clocks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
1.x: Statement 2 is wrong: NavIC (7 satellites – 3 GEO + 4 GSO) times its signals with rubidium atomic clocks. UTC is kept by caesium atomic clocks.

1.s:
Assertion (A): Leap seconds are added to UTC from time to time, as on 31 December 2016.
Reason (R): The Earth's rotation is slowing down.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
1.x: Both are true and R explains A: atomic-clock UTC would drift ahead of the slowing Earth, so leap seconds keep it in step.

1.s: Which of the following longitude is called as international date line?
1.x: The International Date Line runs roughly along the 180° meridian; 0° is the Prime Meridian.

1.s:
Statement (A) : Time interval at the date-line is 12 hours from the Greenwich.
Reason (R) : Date-line is situated at 1800 meridian. Using following options choose the correct answer –
o: (A), (R) both are correct, and (R) is the correct
(A) and (R) both are correct, but (R) is not the correct
1.x: The Date Line lies on the 180° meridian, and 180° × 4 min = 720 min = 12 hours from Greenwich, so R explains A.

1.s: What is the name given to the imaginary line that runs along Earth's surface from the North Pole to the South Pole in the middle of the Pacific Ocean?
1.x: The International Date Line is the imaginary pole-to-pole line along roughly 180° in the middle of the Pacific Ocean, where the date changes.

1.s: Which one of the following straits is nearest to the International Date Line?
1.x: The Date Line passes through the Bering Strait between Russia's Chukchi and Alaska's Seward peninsulas; Malacca, Florida and Gibraltar are far from 180°.

1.s: Which one of the following Straits is nearest to the International Date Line?
1.x: The Bering Strait lies on the 180° Date Line; the other straits are near 100°E, 80°W and 5°W.

1.s: Which path must be followed by a Ship to move from one place to another in the least time ?
1.x:
Book key (UPPCS 1992): along the meridian. Strictly: the least-distance route is a great-circle route, which is a meridian only for places on the same longitude (PMF Human & Economic Geography).
The book key takes the meridian as the least-time path, since meridians are great circles and a great-circle route is the shortest between two points. Currents and sea breezes do not fix a route; 'longitude' only names the angle.

1.s: International Date Line passes through –
1.x: The Date Line runs through the Pacific Ocean along about 180°, bending to avoid land.

1.s: What must a traveller crossing the International Date Line westward, from America to Asia, do to the date?
1.x: Crossing westward a day is added (skipped); crossing eastward a day is subtracted (repeated).

1.s:
Assertion (A): The International Date Line is 12 hours from Greenwich.
Reason (R): The International Date Line roughly follows the 180° meridian.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
1.x: Both are true and R explains A: 180° × 4 min = 720 min = 12 hours. The line runs pole to pole through the middle of the Pacific Ocean.

1.s:
Consider the following statements about the International Date Line:
1. It passes through the Bering Strait, between the Chukchi and Seward peninsulas.
2. It zigzags where land is in the way.
3. A traveller crossing it eastward, from Asia to America, adds a day.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
1.x: Statement 3 is wrong: crossing eastward (Asia → America) one subtracts a day; crossing westward one adds a day. The line passes the Bering Strait between Chukchi (Russia) and Seward (Alaska) and zigzags around Chukotka, the Aleutians, Kiribati, Fiji, Tonga and Samoa.

1.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Big Diomede (Russia) and Little Diomede (USA) lie on opposite sides of the International Date Line, a day apart.
2. Samoa moved to the American side of the Date Line in 2011.
3. Kiribati's Line Islands (UTC+14) are among the first places to see a new day.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
1.x: Statement 2 is wrong: in 2011 Samoa moved to the Asian side of the Date Line. The Diomedes are neighbours a day apart, and Kiribati's Line Islands (UTC+14) see each new day first.

2.s: Apart from Iron and Nickel, which of the following element is an important constituent of inner core of earth?
2.x: Besides iron and nickel, the core's lighter elements are silicon, sulphur and oxygen, so silicon; magnesium, calcium and cobalt are not the light elements cited.

2.s: Which elements are abundant in the formation of interior layer of the earth?
2.x: The core (NIFE) is made of nickel and ferrum (iron); silica–aluminium and silica–magnesium are the SIAL and SIMA layers.

2.s: The upper mantle of earth is made mostly of
2.src: Technical Assistant (Geophysics), Technical Assistants in AP
2.x: The upper mantle is made mostly of silicate minerals (rich in iron and magnesium); molten iron and nickel belong to the outer core.

2.s: This is the largest of all the layers of planet Earth.
2.x: The mantle is the largest layer – about 83% of the Earth's volume and 68% of its mass.

2.s: In the structure of planet Earth, below the mantle, the core is mainly made up of which one of the following?
2.x: The core below the mantle is made mainly of iron (with nickel – NIFE).

2.s: In the structure of planet Earth, below the mantle, the core is mainly made up of which one of the following ?
2.x: The core is mainly iron with nickel; aluminium, chromium and silicon are not its main constituents.

2.s: Which layer lies directly below the mantle?
2.x: The crust is outermost, then the mantle, then the outer core, with the inner core at the centre.
n: Earth’s crust is the outermost layer. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 27-33]
The mantle lies below the crust. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 27-33]
The outer core lies below the mantle. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 27-33]
The inner core is central. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 27-33]
xa: **Crust:** oxygen is the **most abundant** element.
**Outer core** is **liquid** (**2,900–5,150 km**); **inner core** **solid** (**5,150–6,371 km**).
**Moho** separates crust and mantle; **Lehmann** separates outer and inner core.

2.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Compositional layering of the Earth consists of the crust, mantle and core.
2. Mechanical layering of the Earth consists only of the crust, mantle and core.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
2.x: By composition Earth has crust, mantle and core; mechanical layers are lithosphere, asthenosphere, mesosphere, outer core and inner core, so statement 2 is wrong.
n: Compositional layering consists of the crust, mantle, and core. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 27-33]
Mechanical layering consists of the lithosphere, asthenosphere, deeper mantle, outer core, and inner core. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 27-33]
xa: **Lithosphere** = crust + uppermost mantle, about **100 km** thick, **rigid**.
**Asthenosphere** = weak, ductile **low-velocity zone** at ~**100–200 km**.
Layer sequence: Lithosphere → Asthenosphere → Mesosphere → **Barysphere (core)**.

2.s: Why does the inner core remain solid despite the very high temperature prevailing there?
o: Its temperature is lower than that of the crust.
The pressure exerted by the overlying rocks is immense.
It is located outside the mantle.
2.x: The immense pressure caused by the weight of overlying material keeps the inner core solid despite its extreme temperature.
2.tq: Link the physical condition to the controlling factor rather than to temperature alone.
xs: The **immense pressure** of overlying rock keeps the inner core solid — option **(2)**.
Pressure rises with the **weight of overlying rock**.
The inner core is not cooler than the crust — temperature **rises with depth**.
xa: ⚠ Outer core **liquid**, inner core **solid** (pressure).
Core main elements: **iron and nickel** — so option (4) is wrong.

2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the continental crust?
o: It is thicker than the oceanic crust
It is older than the oceanic crust
2.x: Continental crust is thicker, older and granitic; basaltic rock marks the oceanic crust.

2.s: Who gave the terms SIAL, SIMA and NIFE for the layers of the Earth?
2.x: SIAL, SIMA and NIFE are the terms of Suess for the layers by their main elements.

2.s: In Suess's classification, what is the granitic continental layer of silicon and aluminium called?
2.x: SIAL (silicon-aluminium) is granitic and continental; SIMA is basaltic and NIFE the nickel-iron core.
xa: These are **Suess's chemical layers** of the Earth.
The crust's most abundant element is **oxygen (46.6%)**; the whole Earth's is **iron (32.1%)**.

2.s:
Consider the following statements about the layers of the Earth:
1. Oceanic crust is about 5 km thick, while continental crust averages about 30 km.
2. The mantle extends from the Moho down to about 2,900 km.
3. The outer core is a solid layer of iron and nickel.
4. The inner core remains solid because of the immense pressure on it.
How many of the above statements are correct?
2.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the outer core (2,900–5,150 km) is liquid iron–nickel; only the inner core is solid, held so by immense pressure. Oceanic crust is ~5 km and continental ~30 km thick, and the mantle runs from the Moho to ~2,900 km.

2.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The mantle accounts for about 83% of the Earth's volume and 68% of its mass.
2. The core accounts for about 32% of the Earth's volume and 16% of its mass.
3. The mantle is solid but flows plastically, allowing convection.
4. Density rises from about 2.8–3.0 g/cm³ in the crust to about 13.3–13.6 g/cm³ in the inner core.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
2.x: Statement 2 reverses the figures: the core is ~16% of the Earth's volume but ~32% of its mass. The mantle (83% of volume, 68% of mass) is the largest layer, solid but plastic; density climbs from 2.8–3.0 (crust) through ~4.6 (mantle) to 13.3–13.6 g/cm³ (inner core).

2.s:
Match List-I (Layer) with List-II (Composition):
List-I
a. SIAL
b. SIMA
c. NIFE
d. Mantle
List-II
i. Nickel and iron – the core
ii. Silica and aluminium – granitic continents
iii. Mixed metals and silicates – iron–magnesium silicates
iv. Silica and magnesium – basalt, source of magma
2.x: In Suess's scheme SIAL (silica + aluminium) forms the granitic continents, SIMA (silica + magnesium) is basaltic and feeds magma, and NIFE (nickel + ferrum) is the dense core; the mantle is the layer of 'mixed metals and silicates'.

2.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Continental crust is thicker, older and granitic, while oceanic crust is thinner, younger and basaltic.
2. Oceanic crust is lighter than continental crust.
3. By mass, iron is the most abundant element of the Earth as a whole, followed by oxygen and then silicon.
4. Aluminium is one of the main lighter elements of the Earth's core.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
2.x: Statement 2 is wrong: basaltic oceanic crust is denser than granitic continental crust. Statement 4 is wrong: the core's lighter elements are silicon, sulphur and oxygen, not aluminium. Whole-Earth order by mass is iron 32.1% > oxygen 30.1% > silicon 15.1%.

2.s: Which of the following waves are sound waves
o: none of the given answers is correct
2.src: Junior Asst. cum Typist in Prisons and Correctional Services
2.x: P-waves are compressional (longitudinal) waves exactly like sound; on reaching the air they become audible sound. S- and L-waves are not, so 'none of the given answers' is wrong.

2.s: The instrument used to measure earthquakes is
2.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
2.x: A seismograph records earthquake (seismic) waves; a barometer measures air pressure, an altimeter height and a hygrometer humidity.

2.s: Which of the following seismic waves is a longitudinal wave?
2.x: P-waves (primary) are longitudinal push-pull waves; S-waves are transverse and L/Rayleigh waves are surface waves.

2.s: The shadow zone for both P and S waves during an earthquake is
2.x: Neither P nor S waves reach the belt about 105°–145° from the epicentre: S-waves are absent beyond 105° and P-waves are refracted away between ~105° and 145°.

2.s: The tremors produce waves on the surface of the earth which are called seismic waves. They are recorded by an instrument called the seismograph which is a:
2.src: APPSC 2022 Various Non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
2.x: NCERT describes the seismograph as a vibrating rod (or pendulum) that starts vibrating when tremors occur, so 'vibrating rod' is correct; it is not a rotating needle or camera.

2.s: During an earthquake, which type of waves get generated?
2.x: An earthquake generates P (primary), S (secondary) and L (surface) waves – P.S.L; the other letter sets are invented.

2.s: S-waves disappear on reaching the outer core. In what state is the outer core?
2.x: S-waves cannot pass through liquids, so they vanish at the liquid outer core.
n: The outer core is liquid. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 27-33]
S-waves stop in the outer core. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 27-33]
S-waves disappear because the outer core is liquid. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 27-33]
S-waves do not travel through liquids. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 27-33]
S-waves travel through solids only. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 27-33]

2.s: Which seismic waves cause the most damage?
2.x: Surface (L) waves are the slowest but cause the highest damage.

2.s:
Consider the following statements about seismic waves:
1. P-waves are longitudinal (push–pull) waves and arrive first.
2. S-waves are transverse and travel through solids, liquids and gases.
3. Surface (L) waves are the slowest but cause the most damage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
2.x: Statement 2 is wrong: S-waves (transverse, shear) travel through solids only; it is P-waves that pass through solid, liquid and gas. P-waves are fastest and arrive first; surface (Love, Rayleigh) waves are slowest and most damaging.

2.s:
Consider the following statements about the seismic shadow zone:
1. S-waves are absent everywhere beyond about 105° from the epicentre.
2. Direct P-waves are not recorded between roughly 105° and 145° from the epicentre.
3. All earthquakes share one fixed shadow zone, set by the position of the core.
How many of the above statements are correct?
2.x: Statement 3 is wrong: each earthquake has its own shadow zone, set by its epicentre (CGPSC 2020). S-waves vanish beyond ~105°, and P-waves, strongly refracted at the core boundary, leave a gap at ~105°–145° (Rocket: 103°–142°).

2.s:
Assertion (A): The S-wave shadow zone is much larger than the P-wave shadow zone.
Reason (R): S-waves cannot pass through the liquid outer core.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
2.x: Both are true and R explains A: S-waves travel only through solids, so they vanish in the liquid outer core and are absent everywhere beyond ~105°, while P-waves are only refracted, leaving a narrower 105°–145° gap.

2.s:
Assertion (A): Reflection and refraction of seismic waves at boundaries reveal the layers of the Earth's interior.
Reason (R): Seismic waves travel at the same speed in all layers of the Earth.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
2.x: A is true but R is false: wave speed changes with density, and it is this change that causes reflection and refraction at the boundaries, revealing the layers.

2.s: The Earth’s magnetic field is due to :
o: Presence of a huge magnet at is centre
2.x: The geomagnetic field comes from electric currents in the conducting liquid outer core (geodynamo), not from a giant magnet at the centre.

2.s: Isogonic lines pass through points of ____
2.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
2.x: Isogonic lines join points of equal magnetic declination; isoclinic lines join points of equal dip.

2.s: What is the approximate geothermal gradient in the upper crust?
2.x: Temperature rises by approximately 1°C for every 32 m of depth in the upper crust, although the rate slows at greater depths.
2.tq: Pay attention to the place value in the depth-temperature relationship.
xs: In the upper crust temperature rises ~**1°C per 32 m** — option **(1)**.
The rate **slows deeper**.
xa: **Temperature, pressure and density** all rise with depth.
Highest geothermal potential: **Puga Valley** (**Ladakh**).
Other sites: **Manikaran** (HP), **Tattapani** (Chhattisgarh), **Cambay** (Gujarat), **Bakreshwar** (WB).

2.s:
Consider the following statements about the Earth's magnetic field:
1. It is generated by convection of molten iron in the liquid outer core (geodynamo).
2. It shields life from the solar wind and cosmic radiation.
3. The magnetic axis is inclined at about 23½° to the geographic axis.
4. ESA's Swarm mission found that outer-core flow under the Pacific switched from westward to eastward.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
2.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the magnetic axis is inclined about 11.5° to the geographic axis (23½° is the tilt of the Earth's axis). The geodynamo in the liquid outer core makes the field, which shields life; Swarm recorded the switch in flow under the Pacific.

2.s:
Match List-I (Geothermal site) with List-II (State/UT):
List-I
a. Puga Valley
b. Tattapani
c. Cambay
d. Bakreshwar
List-II
i. West Bengal
ii. Chhattisgarh
iii. Ladakh
iv. Gujarat
2.x: Puga Valley is in Ladakh, Tattapani in Chhattisgarh, Cambay in Gujarat and Bakreshwar in West Bengal (Manikaran is in Himachal Pradesh).

2.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Temperature, pressure and density all rise with depth inside the Earth.
2. In the upper crust temperature rises by about 1°C for every 32 m of depth.
3. The Earth's mean density is about 5.5 g/cm³, the highest of all the planets.
4. Diamonds rise from the mantle through kimberlite pipes, and Andhra Pradesh holds about 90% of India's diamond reserves.
How many of the above statements are correct?
2.x: Statement 4 is wrong on the State: Madhya Pradesh holds ~90% of India's diamond reserves, though diamonds do rise through kimberlite pipes. Temperature, pressure and density all rise with depth (~1°C per 32 m in the upper crust); mean density 5.5 g/cm³ makes the Earth the densest planet.

2.s: Which discontinuity separates the outer core from the inner core?
2.x: The Lehmann discontinuity (~5,150 km) separates the outer and inner core; Gutenberg separates the mantle and outer core.

2.s: The Indian plate beneath Tibet has been reported to undergo which process?
o: Subduction of its entire crust into the outer core
Complete melting of its oceanic crust at the surface
Delamination of its dense lower layer into the mantle at about 100 km depth
Separation of its upper layer into the asthenosphere only
2.x: The dense lower layer of the Indian plate is reported to be peeling away and delaminating into the mantle at roughly 100 km depth beneath Tibet.
2.tq: Use the process-location-depth combination to distinguish delamination from subduction.
xs: The Indian plate beneath Tibet is **delaminating** — its dense lower layer peeling into the mantle **~100 km** down — option **(3)**.
Evidence: **94 seismic stations** and **helium isotopes**.
xa: The **lithosphere** (about **100 km**) moves over the **semi-fluid asthenosphere**.
The asthenosphere is the **main source of magma**.
Other recent findings: Stanford's first global map of **continental mantle earthquakes**; Swarm data on outer-core flow.

2.s:
Match List-I (Discontinuity) with List-II (Layers it separates):
List-I
a. Conrad
b. Mohorovicic
c. Repetti
d. Gutenberg
List-II
i. Crust and mantle
ii. Upper and lower mantle
iii. Upper and lower crust
iv. Mantle and outer core
2.x: Conrad (the first from the surface) separates the upper and lower crust (SIAL–SIMA); Moho the crust and mantle; Repetti the upper and lower mantle (~700–1,000 km); Gutenberg the mantle and outer core (~2,900 km), where S-waves vanish. Lehmann separates outer and inner core.

2.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. At the Mohorovicic discontinuity the velocity of P-waves rises from about 6.9 to 8.1 km/s.
2. The discontinuity was identified in 1909 by Andrija Mohorovicic.
3. Andrija Mohorovicic was a German seismologist.
4. The 410 km and 660 km discontinuities mark mineral phase changes in the mantle.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
2.x: Statement 3 is wrong: Mohorovicic was Croatian. At the Moho P-wave speed jumps from 6.9 to 8.1 km/s (found 1909); the 410 km and 660 km levels are mantle mineral phase changes.

2.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The lithosphere is rigid and is broken into plates.
2. The asthenosphere, at about 100–200 km in the upper mantle, is weak, plastic and partly molten.
3. The asthenosphere is the main source of magma.
4. In the sequence lithosphere – asthenosphere – mesosphere – barysphere, the barysphere is the lower mantle.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
2.x: Statement 4 is wrong: the barysphere is the core. The rigid lithosphere (crust + uppermost mantle) is broken into plates that glide over the weak, partly molten asthenosphere (~100–200 km), the main source of magma.

2.s:
Consider the following statements about sources of information on the Earth's interior:
1. The deepest drilled hole, about 12 km, is on the Kola Peninsula.
2. Mponeng and TauTona in South Africa, about 3.9 km deep, are the deepest mines.
3. Meteorites provide direct evidence of the Earth's interior.
4. Gravity anomalies and magnetic surveys are indirect sources.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
2.x: Only statement 3 is wrong: meteorites are indirect evidence, like seismic, gravity and magnetic data. Direct sources are mining, deep drilling (Kola, USSR, ~12 km; Mponeng and TauTona, South Africa, ~3.9 km) and volcanic material.

3.x: Igneous rocks are both crystalline and non-crystalline; they have no fossils (not 'little'), are poorly porous and are made of silicates.

3.x: Rhyolite is felsic extrusive; granite is felsic intrusive, diorite intermediate intrusive and basalt mafic extrusive.
xa: **Gabbro** is the **mafic intrusive** counterpart of basalt.
**Andesite** is another extrusive (volcanic) rock.
Volcanic rocks (**andesite, dacite, rhyolite, basalt**) need more energy to fracture than many sedimentary rocks.

Consider the following statements about igneous rocks:
1. Intrusive rocks such as granite and gabbro cool slowly at depth and have large crystals.
2. Basalt is an extrusive rock formed by the quick cooling of lava.
3. Diorite is a felsic extrusive rock.
4. Mafic rocks are rich in iron, magnesium and calcium, and are dark and dense.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

Assertion (A): Basalt is a fine-grained igneous rock.
Reason (R): Basalt forms when lava cools quickly at the Earth's surface.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
3.x: Both are true and R explains A: extrusive (volcanic) rocks like basalt cool fast at the surface, leaving no time for large crystals to grow, so they are fine-grained.

3.x: Oxygen (46.6%) is the most abundant element in the crust by mass; silicon (27.7%) is second.

3.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
3.x: Bowen's reaction series is the order in which minerals crystallise from cooling magma (olivine first, quartz last).

3.s: What is quartz, a major component of granite and sandstone, chemically?
3.x: Quartz is silicon dioxide (SiO2), hard and resistant to weathering, and a major component of granite and sandstone.
xa: Quartz is a **tectosilicate** (framework), like **albite** and **orthoclase**.
Quartz is the **most stable** mineral of Bowen's series; **olivine** forms first.

3.s: In the discontinuous branch of Bowen's reaction series, which is the first mineral to crystallise?
3.x: The discontinuous branch runs olivine → pyroxene → amphibole → biotite; mafic minerals form first at the highest temperature.
xa: The series ends with **K-feldspar → muscovite → quartz**; **quartz is last** and most stable.
Bowen's series shows the order of **crystallisation from cooling magma** (APPSC **2024**).

3.s: Which of the following pairs (mineral – Mohs hardness) is correctly matched?
3.x: On the Mohs scale topaz is 8; apatite is 5, orthoclase 6 and calcite 3.

3.s:
Consider the following statements about the Earth's crust (by weight):
1. Oxygen, at about 46.6%, is the most abundant element.
2. Silicon, the second most abundant element, is also the most abundant metal.
3. Aluminium, at about 8.1%, is the most abundant metal.
4. Iron, at about 5%, is the second most abundant metal.
How many of the above statements are correct?
3.x: Statement 2 is wrong: silicon (27.7%) is second among elements but is not a metal. Oxygen (46.6%) leads; aluminium (8.1%) is the most abundant metal and iron (5.0%) the second.

3.s:
Consider the following statements about minerals:
1. Feldspar makes up about one-fourth of the Earth's crust.

3.x: Statement 1 is wrong: feldspar makes up about one-half of the crust (NCERT); 'one-fourth' is the APPSC 2024 trap. Quartz (SiO₂) is 7 on the Mohs scale, topaz 8, talc 1; Bowen's series runs from olivine (first) to quartz (last, most stable).

3.s: The rocks in Himalayan Mountains are?
3.x: The Himalayas are folded sedimentary rocks of the Tethys Sea; granite is a rock, not a class, and igneous/metamorphic rocks are only in the core.

3.s: These rocks were used in the construction of Red Fort and Agra Fort in India.
3.x: The Red Fort and Agra Fort are built of red sandstone, a sedimentary rock.

3.s: Coal is an example of –
3.x: Coal is an organically formed sedimentary rock.

3.x: The Himalayas are made primarily of sedimentary rocks (folded Tethys sediments); plutonic rock and dykes occur only locally.

3.s:
Consider the following statements made about the sedimentary rocks:
1. Sedimentary rocks are formed at Earth's surface by the hydrological system.
2. The formation of sedimentary rocks involves the weathering of pre-existing rocks.
3. Sedimentary rocks contain fossils.
4. Sedimentary rocks typically occur in layers. Which of these statements are correct?
3.x: All four are correct: sedimentary rocks form at the surface through the hydrological system, from weathering of older rocks, contain fossils and occur in layers.

3.s:
Consider the following statements:
1.
Statement I: In the context of effect of water on rocks, chalk is known as a very permeable rock whereas clay is known as quite an impermeable or least permeable rock.
2. Statement II: Chalk is porous and hence can absorb water.

Both Statement II and Statement III are correct but only one of them explains Statement I

o: These are such rocks whose structure depend on
These rocks are deposited in layers
These rocks cannot be formed in water

3.x: The age of the Earth is found by uranium (radiometric) dating of the oldest rocks and meteorites; carbon dating works only for young organic remains.

3.s: Who developed the geological time scale in 1760?

Assertion (A): Sedimentary rocks hold most of the fossils.
Reason (R): Sedimentary rocks are formed by the cooling and solidification of magma.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
3.x: A is true but R is false: sedimentary rocks form at the surface from weathered sediments deposited in layers, which preserve remains of organisms; rocks formed from magma are igneous and contain no fossils.

3.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sedimentary rocks cover about 75% of the Earth's surface.
2. Rock salt and gypsum are chemically formed sedimentary rocks.
3. Sandstone, shale and conglomerate are mechanically (clastic) formed sedimentary rocks.
4. Clay is both porous and highly permeable.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
3.x: Statement 4 is wrong: clay is porous but impermeable – its very fine pores are poorly connected (chalk and sandstone are porous and permeable). Sedimentary rocks cover ~75% of the surface; rock salt and gypsum are chemical, sandstone, shale and conglomerate clastic.

3.s: What is Marble?

3.x: Metamorphic rocks form from both igneous and sedimentary rocks under heat and pressure.

3.x: Gneiss is metamorphic; sandstone, limestone and shale are sedimentary, so gneiss is the odd one.

3.x: Granite is igneous; marble, quartzite and slate are metamorphic.

3.x: Quartzite is metamorphosed from quartz-rich sandstone; limestone gives marble and shale gives slate.

(D) Sandstone

Key / textbooks: coal → diamond. Strictly coal metamorphoses to anthracite/graphite; diamonds form from carbon in the mantle, not from coal.
Shale → slate, limestone → marble, coal → diamond (the textbook pairing; strictly graphite), sandstone → quartzite. Moved to rocks.

List-I
a. Shale
b. Granite
c. Basalt
d. Limestone
List-II
i. Marble
ii. Gneiss

3.s:
Consider the following statements about metamorphic rocks:
1. They form from both igneous and sedimentary rocks under heat and pressure.
2. Coal turns into graphite through metamorphism, via anthracite.
3. Garnet and halite are typical metamorphic minerals.
4. Limestone is the odd one out among marble, slate, quartzite and limestone.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
3.x: Statement 3 is wrong: garnet, kyanite and sillimanite are metamorphic minerals but halite is not. Metamorphic rocks come from both igneous and sedimentary rocks; coal ends as graphite; limestone is sedimentary among the metamorphic marble, slate and quartzite.

3.s: Petrology is
3.src: APPSC Group-II Paper-I General Studies & Mental Ability 2019
3.x: Petrology is the study (science) of rocks, a part of geology.

3.s: Lithology primarily refers to the study of which of the following characteristics of a rock unit?
o: Its physical character, including texture, grain size and composition
Its magnetic field and seismic waves
3.x: Lithology describes the physical character of a rock unit, particularly its texture, grain size and composition.
3.tq: Test the precise meaning of a look-alike technical term rather than its broader subject area.
xs: **Lithology** = a rock unit's **physical character** — **texture, grain size, composition** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is not limited to **age** or **fossils**.
xa: **Petrology** is the study of rocks; **uranium dating** fixes the age of very old materials.
**Geological Survey of India**: set up **1851**, under the **Ministry of Mines**.

3.s:
Consider the following statements about the rock cycle:
1. Deposited sediments become sedimentary rock through lithification.
2. Exposed metamorphic rock cannot weather into sediment; it can only melt into magma.
3. Rainwater with dissolved carbon dioxide forms carbonic acid, which weathers rocks.
4. Enhanced rock weathering spreads crushed granite on farmland to lock carbon dioxide as bicarbonate.
How many of the above statements are correct?
3.x: Statements 2 and 4 are wrong: any rock type can become another, and exposed metamorphic rock weathers into sediment; enhanced rock weathering uses crushed basalt. Lithification turns sediment into rock, and carbonic acid from CO₂ in rain weathers rocks.

4.s: Out of the below, India is part of the following land?
4.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
4.x: India was part of Gondwanaland, the southern part of Pangaea – not Laurasia or Eurasia.

4.s: On the earth, originally, there was only one huge landmass which is known as –
4.x: The single original landmass was Pangaea; Panthalassa was the ocean, Laurasia and Gondwanaland its later halves.

4.s: The theory of continental drift was developed by-
4.x: Continental drift was put forward by Alfred Wegener (1912); Hess gave sea-floor spreading and Wilson/Du Toit came later.

4.s: India was the part of ancient Gondwana land Supercontinent. It includes the following landmass of the present :
4.x: Gondwanaland included South America, Africa, Australia (with Antarctica, Madagascar, Arabia, India) – all of the above.

o: More than one of the above
4.x: The southern continent broken from Pangaea is Gondwanaland; Laurasia is the northern one.

4.x: Peninsular India was part of the southern supercontinent Gondwana.

4.x: North America belonged to Laurasia, not Gondwanaland; South America, Africa and Australia were Gondwana.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
4.src: APPSC Group-II Screening Test (General Studies & Mental Abil
4.x: No key: NCERT puts Pangaea's split into Laurasia and Gondwanaland at about 200 million years ago (not 150), while some textbooks use 150 and 65 million years; the official APPSC key could not be found, so neither 'I only', 'II only', 'both' nor 'none' can be confirmed.

4.s:
Which of the following are the evidence of the phenomenon of continental drift?
I. The belt of ancient rocks from Brazil coast matches with those from Western Africa.
II. The gold deposits of Ghana are derived from the Brazil plateau when the two continents lay side by side.
III. The Gondwana system of sediments from India is known to have its counterparts in six different landmasses of the Southern Hemisphere.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
4.x: All three are NCERT evidence: the Brazil–West Africa rock belts, Ghana's gold derived from the Brazil plateau, and the Gondwana sediments with counterparts in six southern landmasses.

4.s:
Assertion (A) : Rich placer deposits of gold are found on the Ghana coast and gold-bearing veins are found in Brazil.
Reason (R) : At some point of time, these continents were joined together along the Atlantic coast.
Select the correct answer.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct
A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
4.x: Both are true and R explains A: Ghana's placer gold has no local source because its source veins are in Brazil, from which it was derived when the continents were joined.

4.s: With which of the following was Wegener's 'pole-fleeing force' associated?
o: The gravity of the Sun and the Moon
4.x: The pole-fleeing force was linked to Earth's rotation and the tidal force to the Sun and Moon; both were too weak, so the theory was not accepted.
xa: **Arthur Holmes** (**1930s**) gave drift the driving force Wegener lacked — **convection currents**.
Wegener proposed continental drift in **1912**.

4.s: What was the name of the mega-ocean that surrounded Pangaea?
4.x: Panthalassa surrounded Pangaea; the Tethys Sea lay between northern Laurasia and southern Gondwanaland.
xa: Laurasia: **North America, Greenland, Europe, Asia (minus India)**.
Gondwanaland: **South America, Africa, India, Australia, Antarctica, Madagascar, Arabia**.

4.s: Gondwana-type tillites in India and their counterparts in southern continents support continental drift. What do tillites indicate?
4.x: Tillites are glacial deposits. Their distribution across India and other southern continents indicates that these areas were formerly connected and experienced common glacial conditions.
4.tq: Identify the process represented by a geological deposit.
xs: **Tillites** are **glacial deposits**, so they indicate **ancient glacial conditions** — option **(1)** is correct.
India's **Gondwana-type tillites** have counterparts in the **other southern continents**, showing they were once joined.
xa: Other evidences: **jig-saw fit**, **same-age rocks**, **placer deposits**, **fossils** (Mesosaurus, Glossopteris).
India belonged to **Gondwanaland**, not Laurasia.

4.s: About how many years ago did Gondwanaland break up?
4.x: Gondwanaland broke up approximately 225 million years ago.
4.tq: Distinguish the geological breakup date from the later Himalayan uplift date.
xs: **Gondwanaland broke up ~225 million years ago** — option **(3)** is correct.
**65 million years ago** is when the **Himalayas rose**, not the break-up.
xa: After the break-up, the **Indian craton** slid towards the **Eurasian craton**.
India moves **north at ~5 cm/year** into the Eurasian plate.

4.s:
Consider the following statements about the continental drift theory:
1. It was put forward by the German scientist Alfred Wegener in 1912.
2. Its proposed forces – the pole-fleeing force and the tidal force – were too weak, so the theory was rejected.
3. Pangaea was surrounded by a mega-ocean called the Tethys.
4. The Tethys Sea separated Laurasia in the north from Gondwanaland in the south.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
4.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the mega-ocean around Pangaea was Panthalassa; the Tethys was the sea between Laurasia and Gondwanaland. Wegener (1912) relied on the pole-fleeing force (rotation) and tidal force (Sun and Moon), which were too weak.

4.s:
Match List-I (Evidence of drift) with List-II (Example):
List-I
a. Jig-saw fit
b. Rock belts
c. Tillite
d. Fossils
List-II
i. Bullard's 1964 computer fit of South America and Africa
ii. About 2,000-million-year-old belt of the Brazil coast matching West Africa
iii. Gondwana glacial sediments of India with counterparts in six southern landmasses
iv. Mesosaurus and Glossopteris
4.x: Bullard's 1964 computer fit is the jig-saw evidence; the ~2,000-million-year rock belts of Brazil match West Africa; tillites are glacial sediments of the Gondwana landmasses; Mesosaurus and Glossopteris are the fossil evidence.

4.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Greenland was a part of Laurasia.
2. Madagascar and Arabia were parts of Gondwanaland.
3. Mesosaurus fossils are found only in India and Australia.
4. The Glossopteris flora is cited as evidence of continental drift.
How many of the above statements are correct?
4.x: Statement 3 is wrong: Mesosaurus fossils occur only in South Africa and Brazil. Laurasia included North America, Greenland, Europe and Asia; Gondwanaland included South America, Africa, India, Australia, Antarctica, Madagascar and Arabia; Glossopteris is fossil evidence of drift.

4.s: The theory that states "pieces of the Earth's crust are in constant, slow motion driven by movement in the mantle" is called:
4.x: 'Pieces of the crust in constant slow motion driven by the mantle' is the theory of plate tectonics.

o: Statement - I and Statement - II both are true
Statement - I and Statement- II both are false
Statement - I is true but Statement - II is false
Statement - I is false but Statement - II is true
4.x: Plate tectonics was put together in 1967 by McKenzie, Parker and Morgan (Hess gave sea-floor spreading), so I is false; it is based on sea-floor spreading, so II is true.

4.s: Based on following statements choose the correct option: Statement - I : Theory of Plate tectonics was given by H.H. Hess in 1967 Statement - II : Theory of Plate Tectonics is based on Theory of Sea floor Spreading
o: Statement - I and Statement - II both are true
Statement - I and Statement- II both are false
Statement - I is true but Statement - II is false
Statement - I is false but Statement - II is true
4.x: Statement I is false (plate tectonics: McKenzie, Parker, Morgan 1967; Hess gave sea-floor spreading); Statement II is true.

4.s: How many plates does the 'theory of Plate Tectonics' consist of?
4.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
4.x: Plate tectonics recognises seven major plates (Pacific, N. American, S. American, Eurasian, African, Indo-Australian, Antarctic).

4.s: Cocos Plate lies between-
4.x: The Cocos Plate lies between Central America and the Pacific Plate; Nazca lies off South America.

4.s: Who proposed the convection current theory as an explanation for the movement of crustal plates?
4.x: Arthur Holmes proposed the convection current theory in the 1930s.
4.tq: Distinguish the proponent of the driving mechanism from proponents of continental drift and sea-floor spreading.
xs: **Arthur Holmes** proposed the **convection current theory** (**1930s**) — option **(4)** is correct.
**Wegener** gave continental drift (**1912**); **Harry Hess** sea-floor spreading (**1961**); **Vine** (with Matthews) explained magnetic stripes (**1963**).
xa: **Radioactive decay heat** in the mantle drives the convection currents.

xa: Example: **Venezuela (M 7.1 and 7.5)** on the Caribbean-South American **strike-slip** boundary.
Toll: **589 dead**.
**USGS** described it as a "seismic doublet" (**26 Jun 2026**).

5.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A seismic doublet is two independent earthquakes of similar magnitude occurring close together in time and place.
2. In June 2026 Caracas, Venezuela, was hit by a seismic doublet of M 7.1 and M 7.5.
3. Harvard University made the first global map of continental mantle earthquakes.
4. Homoseismal (coseismal) lines join places where the shock arrives at the same time.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
5.x: Statement 3 is wrong: Stanford made the first global map of the rare continental-mantle quakes (80+ km below the Moho). The Caracas doublet (M 7.1 and 7.5) struck on 26 June 2026; homoseismal lines join places of equal arrival time (isoseismals join equal intensity).

n: The Koyna earthquake occurred in 1967. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 25-27]

Options:
6.x: Billa Surgam is in Kurnool (now Nandyal) district, not Anantapuramu, so only (a) is incorrect; Belum (Nandyal) is India's second-longest cave and the Kurnool caves with Muchchatla Chintamanu Gavi gave Upper Palaeolithic bone tools.

6.s: ' Arwah ' caves known for its limestone formations and fossils are located in which State of India?

6.s: Which statement correctly describes the cave paintings of Kethavaram?

They are in Visakhapatnam district and exclusively depict cattle.
They are in Kurnool district, where deer is the most painted animal.
They are in Anantapur district and mainly depict horses.
6.x: Kethavaram caves are in Kurnool district, and deer is the most frequently painted animal. A half-painted deer has also been found in Kurnool district.

xs: Kethavaram caves are in **Kurnool district**, where **deer is the most painted animal** — option **(3)**.
A **half-painted deer** has also been found in Kurnool district.
xa: **Billa Surgam** (Nandyal, erstwhile Kurnool): **Palaeolithic** cave site (**APPSC-G2 2025**).
Kurnool caves and **Muchatla Chintamani Gavi** yielded **bone tools** (Upper Palaeolithic).
**Borra** caves have **Mesolithic paintings**.

6.s: Which of the following pairs of caves in Andhra Pradesh are both karst caves?
6.x: Belum and Borra are karstic limestone caves. Undavalli, Bojjannakonda and Erravaram are not karst caves.
xa: **APPSC 2017**: karst among Bojjannakonda, Undavalli, Belum, Erravaram = **Belum**.
Karst = groundwater dissolving **limestone/dolomite**.
Belum = **2nd-longest** natural cave system in India, after **Krem Liat Prah** (Meghalaya).

6.s:
Consider the following statements about the Belum Caves:
1. They are the second-longest natural cave system in India.
2. They were found by Robert Bruce Foote in 1884.
3. They were declared a GSI Geo-Heritage Site in June 2025.
4. They are formed in sandstone.
How many of the above statements are correct?
6.x: Statement 4 is wrong: Belum (Nandyal district) is a karst cave in black limestone with stalactites and stalagmites. It is India's 2nd-longest natural cave (~3.2 km), found by Robert Bruce Foote (1884) and a GSI Geo-Heritage Site (Jun 2025).

6.s:
Match List-I (Cave / site) with List-II (Description):
List-I
a. Undavalli
b. Bojjannakonda
c. Erravaram
d. Krem Liat Prah

6.x: Undavalli is the Vishnukundin rock-cut temple (reclining Vishnu) near Vijayawada; Bojjannakonda at Sankaram (Anakapalli) has Buddhist caves and stupas; Erravaram is a Buddhist site on the Yeleru near Rajahmundry – none is karst. Krem Liat Prah (Meghalaya) is India's longest natural cave.

6.s: Maximum Coastal erosion is caused by :
6.x: Waves are the main agent of coastal erosion (hydraulic action, abrasion); tides, currents and tsunamis play smaller roles.

6.s: Severe coastal erosion in Andhra Pradesh has been particularly reported at which of the following locations?
o: Uppada in Kakinada and the Krishna coast
6.x: Severe coastal erosion has been reported at Uppada in Kakinada and along the Krishna coast. The other options refer to caves, lakes or deltaic features.
6.tq: Use location-based elimination by distinguishing coastal erosion sites from inland landforms and water bodies.
xs: Severe coastal erosion is at **Uppada in Kakinada and the Krishna coast** — option **(3)** (Jul 2026).
Vamsadhara and Penna are **minor deltas**; Borra and Belum are **caves**; Kolleru and Pulicat are **lakes**.
xa: **East coast** erodes more: soft, low-lying **alluvial sand and silt**.
Human causes: harbours, beach sand mining, dredging, **dams**.
Soft defences: beach nourishment, dune stabilisation, **mangroves**.

6.s:
Consider the following statements about coastal erosion:
1. Waves are the main agent of coastal erosion.
2. Saltation is one of the processes of coastal erosion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
6.x: Waves are the main agent; coastal erosion works by hydraulic action, abrasion, attrition and solution. Saltation is a wind process.

6.s: What type of lake is Pulicat in Andhra Pradesh?
6.x: Pulicat is a saltwater lake, whereas Kolleru is a freshwater lake.
xa: Pulicat is a **lagoon** formed by a bar closing a bay.
Minor deltas: **Vamsadhara** and **Penna**.
Coastal erosion: **Uppada** (Kakinada), Krishna coast.

6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Dalmatian and ria coasts?
o: In a Dalmatian coast, mountain ranges run parallel to the coast.
Drowning of a Dalmatian coast produces long islands and channels parallel to the shore.
In a ria coast, mountain ranges run parallel to the shore.
Croatia on the Adriatic is associated with the Dalmatian coast.
6.x: In a ria coast the ranges generally lie at right angles to the shore; parallel ranges characterise the Dalmatian coast.
xa: **Ria** = drowned **river** valley — **NW Spain**.
**Fiord** = drowned **glacial** valley — **Norway**.
⚠ **Ria** = right angles; **Dalmatian** = parallel.

6.s: Where is Erra Matti Dibbalu, a site of late-Quaternary red dunes, located?
6.x: Erra Matti Dibbalu are late-Quaternary red dunes in Visakhapatnam; in September 2025 the site was added to UNESCO's Tentative List.
xa: Collector ordered **tourism upgrades** at Erra Matti Dibbalu (15 May 2026).
Belum = **Geo-Heritage Site by GSI** (Jun 2025).
Wind landforms include **sand dunes** and **loess**.

6.s: What type of natural feature is Tirumala Silathoranam, on the UNESCO Tentative List?
6.x: Tirumala Silathoranam is a quartzite arch; with Erra Matti Dibbalu it is on the UNESCO Tentative List (Sep 2025).

6.s: Chilika and Pulicat are examples of which coastal landform?
6.x: Chilika and Pulicat are lagoons: shallow water cut off from the sea by a bar.

6.s:
Match List-I (Coastal landform) with List-II (Formation):
List-I
a. Stack
b. Spit
c. Tombolo
d. Lagoon
List-II
i. Bar joining an island to the mainland
ii. Shallow water cut off from the sea by a bar
iii. Ridge of sand joined to the land at one end
iv. Left standing when a sea arch collapses
6.x: Erosion runs sea cave → arch → stack → stump, the stack being left when the arch collapses; a spit is a ridge joined to the land at one end (longshore drift); a tombolo joins an island to the mainland; a lagoon is shallow water cut off by a bar (Chilika, Pulicat).

6.s:
Consider the following statements about coastal defence:
1. Groynes are built across the longshore drift to trap sand.
2. Beach nourishment is a hard defence measure.
3. Dams, harbours and sand mining cut the sediment supply and worsen coastal erosion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
6.x: Statement 2 is wrong: beach nourishment, like dunes and mangroves, is a soft defence; seawalls, groynes and breakwaters are hard defences. Groynes trap sand across the longshore drift, and dams, harbours and sand mining starve beaches of sediment.

6.s:
Assertion (A): The east coast of India suffers more coastal erosion than the west coast.
Reason (R): The east coast is made of soft, low alluvium with no rocky cliffs.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
6.x: Both are true and R explains A: the east coast's soft, low alluvium without rocky cliffs erodes easily – severe at Uppada (Kakinada) and on the Krishna coast.

6.s:
Consider the following statements about coasts:
1. A fiord coast is a drowned glacial valley, as in Norway.
2. On a Dalmatian coast the ranges run parallel to the shore, as on the Adriatic.
3. The Coromandel coast is an emergent coast with many natural ports.
4. The Konkan coast was submerged by faulting.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the emergent east (Coromandel) coast has a broad plain but few natural ports. Fiords are drowned glacial valleys (Norway), Dalmatian ranges run parallel to the coast (Adriatic), and the Konkan coast is submerged by faulting.

6.s: The landform of 'Hanging Valley' is associated with which of the following geomorphic process?
6.x: A hanging valley is left high above a main valley deepened by a larger glacier, joining it by a waterfall – a glacial landform.

6.s: Drumlins are found in?
6.x: Drumlins are inverted-boat-shaped mounds of glacial till, so they are found in glaciated areas such as Himalayan glaciers, not oceans, deserts or deltas.

6.s: A field of drumlins gives rise to which type of topography?
6.x: Drumlins are oval, egg-shaped hills of till, and a field of them gives 'basket of eggs' topography.
xa: Some notes attach "basket of eggs" to **boulder deposits**.
**Esker** = stratified ridge from a sub-glacial tunnel.
Till, moraine and boulder clay = **glacial activity** (**APPSC 2017**).

6.s:
Consider the following statements about glacial deposits:
1. A moraine consists of unsorted debris.
2. An esker consists of stratified sediment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
6.x: Both are correct: moraine (till) is unsorted, while an esker is a ridge of stratified sediment from a sub-glacial tunnel.

6.s:
Match List-I (Glacial landform) with List-II (Meaning):
List-I
a. Cirque
b. Arête
c. Horn
d. Fjord
List-II
i. Knife-edged ridge between two cirques
ii. Armchair-shaped hollow at the head of a valley
iii. Sharp pyramidal peak such as the Matterhorn
iv. Drowned glacial U-shaped valley
6.x: A cirque (corrie) is the armchair hollow at the valley head; an arête is the knife-edged ridge between two cirques; a horn is a pyramidal peak (Matterhorn); a fjord is a drowned glacial U-valley (Norway, Greenland, New Zealand).

6.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A U-shaped valley forms when a glacier deepens and widens a river valley.
2. An esker is a winding ridge of unsorted till dumped at the snout of a glacier.
3. Hanging glaciers are stranded on steep slopes as the main glacier thins.
4. From 2025 the Central Water Commission monitors 902 glacial lakes and water bodies.
How many of the above statements are correct?
6.x: Statement 2 is wrong: an esker is a winding ridge of stratified meltwater sediment from a sub-glacial tunnel (unsorted till forms moraines). Statement 4 is wrong: CWC now monitors 2,843 glacial lakes/water bodies, up from 902. Statements 1 and 3 are correct.

6.s:
Assertion (A): A hanging valley commonly joins the main glacial valley through a waterfall.
Reason (R): The main glacier deepens its valley far more than the tributary glacier, leaving the tributary valley high above it.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
6.x: Both are true and R explains A: the main glacier deepens its valley more, so the tributary valley is left hanging high above it and joins it by a waterfall (Yosemite); the agent is the glacier.

6.s: Which of the following is not an Erosional Land form of Wind?
6.x: Barchans are crescent dunes built by wind deposition; yardangs, inselbergs and ventifacts are erosional.

6.s: Barchans and semi-circular sand dunes are found in this region of India
6.x: Barchans and crescent dunes are common in the Thar around Jaisalmer, Rajasthan; the Gobi is not in India and Bhongir is a granite hill. Printed key was missing.

6.s: Land forms in desert are formed mainly due to
6.src: Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare 2017
6.x: Desert landforms are made mainly by wind – deflation, abrasion and deposition (dunes, yardangs, mushroom rocks).

6.s:
Assertion (A): A sand dune is an accumulation of sand.
Reason (R): Sand dunes result from wind deposition.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
6.x: Both are true and R explains A: wind dropping its sand is what builds the dune.
6.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Wind deposition forms sand dunes. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
Sand dunes are accumulations of sand. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
Wind forms sand dunes. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
xs: **Both A and R are true**, and R is the **correct explanation** of A — option **(1)**.
**Sand dunes** are **accumulations of sand** produced by **wind deposition**.
xa: **Barchans** = **crescent-shaped** dunes; **seif** = **long, narrow** ridges.
**Loess** is also a wind-deposited **fine silt**.
Erosional wind forms: **mushroom rock**, **zeugen**, **yardang**.
**Erra Matti Dibbalu** (Visakhapatnam) — late-Quaternary red dunes on UNESCO's Tentative List.

6.s: What is a flat-topped table hill of arid regions called?
6.x: A mesa is a flat-topped table hill; a butte is a smaller remnant and an inselberg an isolated residual hill.

6.s:
Match List-I (Arid landform) with List-II (Key point):
List-I
a. Seif
b. Mushroom rock
c. Playa
d. Barchan
List-II
i. Dry salt-lake bed left by evaporation
ii. Long, narrow longitudinal dune where sand is scarce
iii. Crescent dune with horns pointing downwind
iv. Base abraded by wind more than the top
6.x: Seifs are long narrow dunes where sand is scarce; a mushroom rock forms because wind abrades its base more than its top; a playa is the dry salt bed of an evaporated desert lake; a barchan is a crescent dune with horns downwind (Thar, Jaisalmer).

6.s:
Consider the following statements about aeolian landforms:
1. A yardang is a streamlined ridge lying parallel to the wind.
2. A zeugen is a table-like ridge with a soft cap over hard rock.
3. Uluru is an inselberg, an isolated residual hill.
4. Loess is fine wind-blown silt, as on the Loess Plateau of China.
How many of the above statements are correct?
6.x: Statement 2 is wrong: a zeugen has a hard cap over soft rock, which is why it stands as a table-like ridge. Yardangs parallel the wind, Uluru is an inselberg and loess is fine wind-blown silt (China).

6.s:
Match the following:
List I (Landform) a. Delta b. Cirque c. Cliffs d. Sand Dunes
List II (Geomorphic agent) I. Waves and Currents II. Winds III. Running water IV. Glaciers
6.x: Delta – running water, cirque – glaciers, cliffs – waves and currents, sand dunes – winds: a-III, b-IV, c-I, d-II.

6.s: By which agents are coastal landforms such as cliffs, arches and stacks formed?
6.x: Cliffs, caves, arches, stacks and beaches are coastal landforms made by waves, currents and tides.
xa: Desert landforms: **dunes**, **yardangs**, **mushroom rocks**, **playas**, **loess**.
Coastal landforms also include **caves**, **beaches**, **spits**, **lagoons**.
Karst landforms form by **solution of limestone**.

6.s: Which of the following pairs of landform and its type is correctly matched?
6.x: Yardangs are desert landforms formed by wind; playas, loess and mushroom rocks are also desert (wind) landforms.
n: Desert landforms are formed by wind erosion and deposition. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
Dunes are desert landforms. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
Yardangs are desert landforms. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
Mushroom rocks are desert landforms. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
Playas are desert landforms. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
Loess is a desert landform. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]

6.s: Which one of the following pairs is incorrectly matched?
6.x: An esker is a glacial depositional feature. Yardang and mushroom rock are aeolian features, while a peneplain is associated with prolonged fluvial denudation.
6.tq: Use the wrong-agent trap in a geomorphic-landform pairing.
xs: **Esker — Waves and currents** is wrong — option **(1)**: an esker is a **glacier** landform.
Esker = long, winding ridge of **stratified** sediment marking a **sub-glacial tunnel**.
**Mushroom rock** and **yardang** — wind; **peneplain** — running water: correct.
xa: ⚠ **Moraine** = unsorted; **esker** = stratified.
Waves and currents make **cliff, stack, spit, bar**.
Peninsular plateau = **rejuvenated peneplain**.

6.s: By which process are rift valleys such as Death Valley and the Narmada valley formed?
6.x: Rift valleys, horsts and grabens are formed by tectonic faulting.

6.s:
Match List-I (Agent) with List-II (Landforms):
List-I
a. Running water
b. Glaciers
c. Groundwater
d. Tectonic faulting
List-II
i. Sinkholes, stalactites and blind valleys
ii. Delta, V-valley, gorge and canyon
iii. Rift valleys such as Death Valley and the Narmada
iv. Cirque, arête, horn and moraine
6.x: Deltas, V-valleys, gorges and canyons are made by running water; cirques, arêtes, horns and moraines by glaciers; sinkholes, stalactites and blind valleys by groundwater (karst); rift valleys such as Death Valley and the Narmada by tectonic faulting.

6.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mountains are formed by folding, faulting, volcanism and erosion.
2. The Alps, Andes and Rockies are young fold mountains.
3. The Aravallis and the Urals are young fold mountains.
4. Valleys are formed by river, glacier, tectonic and karst processes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the Aravallis and Urals are old fold mountains (with the Appalachians and Pennines); the Alps, Andes, Rockies and Himalayas are young. Mountains come from folding, faulting, volcanism and erosion; valleys from river, glacier, tectonic and karst processes.

Act as earth's shield and absorbing harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun
To trap heat and keep the earth warm

The layer about 10-20 km. below the surface of Earth

To prevent ultra-violet radiation effect on the ground

7.s:

7.x: Ozone concentration is maximum in the stratosphere (~90% of all ozone).

o: Provides safety to life on earth from ultraviolet

7.x: The ozone layer protects life from the Sun's harmful UV; the troposphere, ionosphere and mist do not.

It prevents the Sun’s ultraviolet rays from reaching

7.s: Excessive ultraviolet exposure due to ozone depletion is associated with which eye disorder?
7.x: Increased UV exposure is associated with cataract, as well as skin cancer, immune suppression and lower crop yield.
xa: The ozone layer absorbs **UV-B and UV-C**.
Ozone depletion is driven by **halocarbons** (**CFCs, HCFCs**).
The **Montreal Protocol** (**1987**) controls nearly **100** ODS.

7.s:
Assertion (A): Temperature increases with altitude in the stratosphere.
Reason (R): Ozone absorbs ultraviolet radiation and converts solar energy into heat.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
7.x: Both are true and R explains A: ozone absorbs ultraviolet rays and turns them into heat, so the stratosphere warms with height.
7.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Temperature increases with altitude in the stratosphere. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 42-50]
Ozone absorbs ultraviolet radiation in the stratosphere. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 42-50]
Absorption of ultraviolet radiation converts solar energy into heat. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 42-50]
Conversion of solar energy into heat causes temperature to increase upward in the stratosphere. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 42-50]
xs: **Both A and R are true**, and R is the **correct explanation** of A — option **(1)**.
**Ozone absorbs ultraviolet radiation**, **converting solar energy into heat**, so **temperature increases upward** in the stratosphere.
⚠ In the **troposphere** temperature **decreases** upward.
xa: The stratosphere extends up to **50 km**; it is an **inversion** layer.
It has **very little water vapour** and is **suitable for jet aircraft**.
An **ozone molecule** has **three oxygen atoms**.

7.s:
Consider the following statements about ozone:
1. About 90% of all atmospheric ozone lies in the stratosphere.
2. In the Chapman cycle, ultraviolet radiation splits O₂ and the oxygen atoms combine with O₂ to form O₃.
3. Column ozone is measured in Dobson Units, one Dobson Unit being 1 mm of pure ozone at 0°C and 1 atm.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: Statement 3 is wrong: 1 DU = 0.01 mm of pure ozone at 0°C and 1 atm, not 1 mm. About 90% of ozone is stratospheric (~10% tropospheric), and the Chapman cycle is UV + O₂ → O + O; O + O₂ → O₃.

7.s:
Consider the following statements about ultraviolet radiation and the ozone layer:
1. UV-A (315–400 nm) mostly reaches the Earth's surface.
2. UV-B (280–315 nm) is completely absorbed by the ozone layer.
3. UV-C (100–280 nm) is the shortest and most harmful band.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
7.x: Statement 2 is wrong: UV-B is mostly absorbed but part of it reaches the ground; it is UV-C, the shortest and most harmful band, that the ozone layer absorbs completely (APPSC FSO 2025). UV-A mostly reaches the surface.

7.s:
Consider the following statements about ozone:
1. Ground-level ozone is a secondary pollutant formed from NOx and VOCs in sunlight.
2. Heatwaves raise ground-level ozone in north-west India and the Indo-Gangetic Plain.
3. Ground-level ozone, like stratospheric ozone, protects living organisms from UV-B.
How many of the above statements are correct?
7.x: Statement 3 is wrong: only stratospheric ozone is the protective shield; ground-level (tropospheric) ozone is a harmful secondary pollutant of photochemical smog, formed from NOx and VOCs in sunlight and raised by heatwaves.

7.s: Which of the following has no direct role in the ozone layer depletion?

7.x: CFCs release chlorine that destroys ozone; UV rays are absorbed by ozone (they do not deplete it), and heavy metals or reactive oxygen species are not the cause.

7.s: What is the primary cause of ozone depletion in the stratosphere?
7.src: APPSC 2023 Lecturers in Government Degree Colleges
7.x: Halocarbons (CFCs, HCFCs, halons) release chlorine and bromine that destroy stratospheric ozone; CO2, methane and water vapour do not.

7.s: What impact does the increase in halocarbon gases, such as chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), have on the environment?
o: They increase ozone levels in the stratosphere
7.src: APPSC 2023 Lecturers in Government Degree Colleges
7.x: Halocarbons such as CFCs deplete the stratospheric ozone layer; they do not stop warming (they are GHGs) or raise ozone.

7.s: Depletion of Ozone layer is caused by
7.src: APPSC 2025 Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer in Sainik Welfare Se
7.x: CFCs release chlorine that destroys ozone; UV rays are absorbed by ozone, not the cause of its loss.

7.s: The formation of ozone holes in the Antarctic Region has been a cause of concern. What could be the reason for the formation of this hole?
o: Presence of prominent tropospheric turbulence, and inflow of chlorofluorocarbons
Presence of prominent polar front and stratospheric clouds; and inflow of chlorofluorocarbons
Absence of polar front and stratospheric clouds; and inflow of methane and chlorofluorocarbons
Increased temperature at polar region due to global warming
7.x: A strong polar vortex (polar front) isolates very cold air where polar stratospheric clouds form; their surfaces activate chlorine from CFCs, which destroys ozone in spring.

7.s: The formation of the ozone hole in the Antarctic region has been a cause of concern. What could be the reason for the formation of this hole?
o: Presence of prominent tropospheric turbulence and
Presence of prominent polar front and stratospheric
Absence of polar front and stratospheric clouds and
Increased temperature in the polar region due to global
7.x: The Antarctic ozone hole forms because of a prominent polar front (vortex) and polar stratospheric clouds acting on chlorine from CFCs.

7.s: Which is responsible for Ozone Hole?
7.x: CFCs are responsible for the ozone hole; CO2, SO2 and O2 are not ozone-depleting.

7.s: The Pollutants causing maximum damage to the ozone layer are –
7.x: Chlorofluorocarbons cause the maximum damage to the ozone layer.

7.s: Formation of the ozone hole is maximum over –
7.x: The ozone hole is largest over Antarctica in the southern spring (Aug–Nov).

7.s: The presence of which of the following degrades ozone from ozonosphere?
7.x: CFCs degrade ozone in the ozonosphere; CO, CO2 and nitrogen do not.

7.s: Over which of the following regions is the major ozone hole of the Earth?
7.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
7.x: The ozone hole forms over Antarctica every southern spring, when polar stratospheric clouds help chlorine destroy ozone; the Arctic loss is much smaller. Moved to the atmosphere row.

7.s: The largest ozone hole is observed over
7.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
7.x: The largest (seasonal) ozone hole lies over Antarctica, not over Africa, Australia or India. Moved to the atmosphere row.

7.s: Which one of the following correctly compares CFCs and HFCs?
o: CFCs spare ozone, whereas HFCs destroy ozone and have no warming effect.
CFCs destroy stratospheric ozone and are potent greenhouse gases; HFCs spare ozone but have high global-warming potential.
Both CFCs and HFCs destroy stratospheric ozone to the same extent.
Neither CFCs nor HFCs has any significant effect on the atmosphere.
7.x: CFCs deplete stratospheric ozone and act as potent greenhouse gases. HFCs do not harm ozone but have high global-warming potential.
7.tq: Use the contrasting ozone and warming effects to separate the two confusable groups.
xs: **CFCs** destroy **stratospheric ozone** and are potent GHGs; **HFCs** spare ozone but have **high GWP** — option **(2)**.
CFCs have a **GWP 1,000-23,000** and make up **15%** of the enhanced effect.
xa: HFCs **replaced CFCs**.
**Kigali Amendment** (**2016**, in force **2019**) cuts HFCs by **80-85%**.
It could avoid up to **0.5°C** of warming by **2100**.

7.s: From where was Mission SANA, India's first indigenous stratospheric super-pressure balloon, launched?
7.x: Mission SANA by Red Balloon Aerospace, India's first home-made stratospheric super-pressure balloon, was launched from Vijayawada in May 2026.

7.s:
Consider the following statements about ozone-depleting substances:
1. HCFCs also deplete ozone.
2. HFCs spare ozone but have high global-warming potential.
3. Halons are used as fumigants.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
7.x: HCFCs deplete ozone and HFCs spare it but warm the climate; halons are used in fire extinguishers, methyl bromide is the fumigant.

7.s:
Match List-I (Ozone-depleting substance) with List-II (Use):
List-I
a. CFCs
b. Halons
c. Methyl bromide
d. Carbon tetrachloride
List-II
i. Refrigeration, air-conditioners and aerosols
ii. Fire extinguishers
