Statement II: The Bay of Bengal branch causes heavy rainfall in Meghalaya.
o: None of the statements is correct
16.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
16.x: Both are correct: Kerala is the first state to receive the SW monsoon in early June, and the Bay of Bengal branch gives very heavy orographic rain in Meghalaya.

16.s: Which of the following regions is not affected much by the Arabian Sea branch of Monsoon?
16.x: The Arabian Sea branch soaks the Western Ghats, the Deccan and Madhya Pradesh (via the Narmada–Tapi valleys); the Chhattisgarh Basin gets its rain mainly from the Bay of Bengal branch.

16.s: By which monsoon does Jharkhand receive rainfall?
16.x: Jharkhand gets most of its rain from the south-west monsoon (Bay of Bengal branch), June–September.

16.s: Monsoon season extends from?
16.x: The SW monsoon season is June–September; in the north it is effectively mid-June to mid-September.

16.s: On which date did the south-west monsoon set in over Kerala in 2026?
16.x: In 2026, the monsoon reached Kerala on 4 June, which was three days later than the normal date.
16.tq: Distinguish the Kerala onset date from the later Andhra Pradesh onset date.
xs: In **2026** the monsoon set in over Kerala on **4 June** — option **(1)** — **three days late** under a strengthening **El Nino**.
**1 June** is the normal Kerala onset date; **6 June** is when it reached **AP**.
xa: **17 of 28** AP districts were deficient by **14 June**.
The onset forecast (26 May ± **4** days) failed — first miss since **2015**.
Normally **A&N Islands ~25 May**, then **Kerala ~1 June**; full coverage by **8 July** (revised normal).

16.s:
Consider the following statements about the heavy rainfall of India's western coast:
1. It is caused by moist Arabian Sea winds striking the Western Ghats.
2. It is of the convectional type.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
16.x: Arabian Sea winds rise over the Western Ghats and give orographic rain, not convectional rain.
n: The Western Coast receives the heaviest rainfall. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 49-53]
The Arabian Sea branch of the Southwest Monsoon causes heavy rainfall on the Western Coast. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 49-53]
Moist winds strike the Western Ghats. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 49-53]
The Western Ghats produce orographic rainfall. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 49-53]
The Western Ghats and the west coast receive the heaviest rainfall. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 49-53]
The Western Coast receives rainfall from the Arabian Sea branch in association with the Western Ghats. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 49-53]

16.s:
Assertion (A): Meghalaya receives very heavy rainfall.
Reason (R): The Bay of Bengal branch and orographic uplift contribute to rainfall in Meghalaya.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
16.x: Both are true and R explains A: Bay of Bengal winds forced up the funnel-shaped Meghalaya hills drop very heavy rain.
16.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: The Bay of Bengal branch causes very heavy rainfall in Meghalaya. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 49-53]
Orographic uplift causes very heavy rainfall in Meghalaya. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 49-53]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
**Meghalaya** receives **very heavy rainfall** from the **Garo**, **Khasi** and **Jaintia Hills**.
It is caused by the **Bay of Bengal branch** and **orographic uplift**.
xa: **Mawsynram** and **Cherrapunji** both get rain by orographic uplift.
Meghalaya is the **highest-rainfall state**; Rajasthan the lowest.

2. The east coast of India produces more rice than the west coast.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
16.x: The west coast gets more rain (narrow plain, high Ghats), but the east coast grows more rice because of its climate and soil.

16.s:
Consider the following statements about the onset of the south-west monsoon:
1. Its sudden onset in the first week of June is called the 'burst' of the monsoon.
2. The IMD declares onset over Kerala after 10 May when 60% of 14 stations record 2.5 mm of rain on two consecutive days.
3. The monsoon lasts for more than 120 days in west Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
16.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the monsoon lasts more than 120 days in the south-west peninsula but less than 75 days in west Rajasthan, which it reaches last. Statements 1 and 2 are correct.

16.s:
Consider the following statements about the Arabian Sea branch of the south-west monsoon:
1. After the Western Ghats it reaches central India through the Narmada–Tapi valleys.
2. Rajasthan gets scanty rain because one arm of it runs parallel to the Aravallis.
3. The Chhattisgarh Basin receives most of its rain from this branch.
4. The majority of the monsoon winds enter Tamil Nadu through the Palghat Gap.
How many of the above statements are correct?
16.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the Chhattisgarh Basin is not much affected by the Arabian Sea branch (it gets Bay branch rain). Statement 4 is wrong: only part of the branch passes through the Palghat Gap. Statements 1 and 2 are correct, so only two.

16.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Bay of Bengal branch strikes the funnel-shaped Garo–Khasi–Jaintia hills, giving heavy orographic rain at Mawsynram and Cherrapunji.
2. Deflected westward by the Himalayas, the Bay branch gives rain that increases from east to west along the Ganga plain.
3. A 'break' in the monsoon occurs when the monsoon trough shifts north to the Himalayan foothills.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
16.x: Only statement 2 is wrong: along the Ganga plain the Bay branch rain DECREASES from east to west. Statements 1 and 3 are correct – Meghalaya's orographic rain from the Bay branch, and breaks when the trough (ITCZ) moves to the Himalayan foothills (plains dry, hills wet).

16.s: In North India, heat waves normally occur in the following period?
16.x: IMD's heat-wave season over north India runs from March to June (peak May–June); the shorter spans leave out part of it.

16.s: Arrange the following seasons in Chronological order according to Hindu Calendar : (i) Autumn (ii) Summer (iii) Spring (iv) Rainy Select the correct answer using the code given below:
16.x: The six seasons run Vasanta (spring, Mar–Apr), Grishma (summer, May–Jun), Varsha (rainy, Jul–Aug), Sharad (autumn, Sep–Oct), so the order is (iii), (ii), (iv), (i).

16.s: Hot weather season thunderstorms associated with violent winds and torrential down pours in West Bengal are also called as
16.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer in Sainik Welfare Service
16.x: The violent pre-monsoon evening thunderstorms of West Bengal are Kaal Baisakhi (Nor'westers). Mango showers are in Kerala–Karnataka, and Loo is a hot dry wind.

16.s: Which of the following is a local storm of Bengal and Assam, useful for tea and rice cultivation ?
16.x: Norwesters (Kaal Baisakhi) are the local storms of Bengal and Assam that help tea, jute and rice. Mango and blossom showers are South Indian; Karaburan is a Central Asian wind.

16.s: Mango showers are common phenomena in which States of India?
16.x: Mango showers are the pre-monsoon showers of Kerala and coastal Karnataka that help mangoes ripen.

16.s: From the following states, which one usually witnesses the blossom shower?
16.x: Blossom showers are pre-monsoon showers of Kerala (and Karnataka) that make coffee flowers blossom.

16.s: What does 'Nautapa' refer to?
o: A prolonged break in the northeast monsoon
A nine-day period of winter rainfall in south India
The first week of the southwest monsoon in Kerala
A nine-day period of peak summer heat in north India before the monsoon
16.x: Nautapa is the traditional nine-day peak of summer heat in north India and occurs just before the arrival of the monsoon.
16.tq: Identify a traditional climatic term by its duration, season and region.
xs: **Nautapa** is the traditional **nine-day** peak of **summer heat** in **north India**, just before the monsoon — option **(4)**.
It is not a rainy spell or a monsoon break.
xa: Heat waves peak in **May-June**.
Record: **Ganganagar** ~**50°C** (**1935**).
Onset over **Kerala ~1 June**.

16.s: Which of the following traditional Indian seasons is INCORRECTLY matched with its months?
16.x: Autumn is September–October; November–December is the pre-winter season. The other three pairs are correct.
n: The Indian traditional summer season lasts from May to June. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 19-27]
The Indian traditional rainy season lasts from July to August. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 19-27]
The Indian traditional autumn season lasts from September to October. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 19-27]
The Indian traditional pre-winter season lasts from November to December. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 19-27]
The Indian traditional winter season lasts from January to February. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 19-27]
xa: **Spring** = **March to April**.
Six traditional seasons: **Vasanta**, **Grishma**, **Varsha**, **Sharad**, **Hemanta**, **Shishira**.
⚠ IMD seasons differ: SW monsoon **June-September**, post-monsoon **October-December**.

16.s: As per the IMD classification, which months does the south-west monsoon season cover?
16.x: The IMD south-west monsoon season is June–September; October–December is the post-monsoon season.
xa: **Post-monsoon / NE monsoon** = **October-December**.
Older notes use **Dec-Feb** for winter; coldest months **Dec-Jan**.
Hottest in NW/central India: **April-June**; heat waves peak **May-June**.

16.s: As per the IMD, which months does the pre-monsoon (hot weather) season cover?
16.x: IMD's pre-monsoon or hot-weather season is March–May.

1. The south-west monsoon season is June–September.
2. The post-monsoon season is October–December.
3. The winter season is November–February.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
16.x: The SW monsoon is June–September and the post-monsoon October–December; IMD winter is January–February.

16.s: With which State are the Kaal Baisakhi (Nor'westers) mainly associated?
16.x: Kaal Baisakhi strikes West Bengal (also Odisha and Assam) in the hot season (APPSC GS 2025 key). Kerala gets mango showers, while Rajasthan and Punjab get the Loo and Andhi dust storms.

xs: **Kaal Baisakhi** strikes **West Bengal** — option **(2)** (APPSC GS 2025 key).
It also hits **Odisha and Assam**; **Kerala** gets **mango showers**; Rajasthan and Punjab get **Loo** and **Andhi**.

In Assam: "**tea showers**", locally **Bardoli Chheerha**.
**Blossom showers** aid **coffee** flowering.

2. They are rare during the monsoon season.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
16.x: Hailstorms in India occur mainly in the pre-monsoon season (March–May) and in winter, not October–December, and are rare during the monsoon.

Hailstorms are rare in India during the monsoon. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 39-41]

16.s: In 2026, a June rainfall deficit of about how much led the Centre to activate monsoon contingency plans?
16.x: A 43% June deficit led to contingency planning; the IMD forecast was about 90% of the long-period average.
xa: April forecast was **92% of LPA** — first "below normal" April forecast in **11 years**.
**August 2026** was the hottest August; four Bay lows lasted **26 days** (normal **16.3**).
Onset over Kerala on **4 June**, **3** days late.

16.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
a. Thermal (differential heating) theory
b. Dynamic (ITCZ) theory
c. Southern Oscillation
d. MONEX, 1979
List-II
1. Gilbert Walker
2. Edmund Halley
3. WMO experiment that confirmed the role of the shifting ITCZ
4. Northward shift of the ITCZ over the Ganga plain as the monsoon trough
16.x: Edmund Halley (1686) gave the thermal theory – land heats faster than sea (a-2); the dynamic theory explains the monsoon by the ITCZ moving north over the Ganga plain (b-4); Gilbert Walker described the Southern Oscillation in the 1920s (c-1); MONEX 1979 under the WMO confirmed the role of the shifting ITCZ (d-3).

16.s:
Consider the following statements about the monsoon mechanism:
1. The Tropical Easterly Jet extends from the South China Sea towards East Africa during the south-west monsoon.
2. Heavy snow cover on the Tibetan Plateau strengthens the south-west monsoon.
3. The Somali jet, along with the Somalia Current, strengthens the monsoon.
4. The Mascarene High near Madagascar drives the cross-equatorial flow.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
16.x: Statement 2 is wrong: a heated Tibetan Plateau (summer heat island, upper-air anticyclone) strengthens the TEJ and the monsoon, but heavy snow cover WEAKENS it. Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct.

16.s:
Assertion (A): El Nino years are generally associated with a weak monsoon and drought-like conditions in parts of India.
Reason (R): El Nino is a cold current that appears off the coast of Peru every 3–7 years.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
16.x: A is true: El Nino weakens and delays the monsoon (a positive IOD can offset it). R is false: El Nino is a WARM current that replaces the cold Peruvian current off Peru every 3–7 years.

16.x: Statement 4 is wrong: the Bharat Forecast System under Mission Mausam has a 6 km resolution (10-day rainfall forecasts). Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct, so only three.

19.s: Teak wood trees grow in the following type of forests
19.x: Teak is a deciduous tree: it dominates the tropical moist deciduous forests and also grows in the dry deciduous belt, so 'tropical deciduous forests' is the best answer. It does not grow in temperate or beach forests, and 'dry deciduous' covers only part of its range.

19.s: In India, in which one of the following types of forests is teak a dominant tree species?
19.x: Teak is the dominant tree of the tropical moist deciduous forests, which have a wet monsoon season followed by a distinct dry season. It is not a rain-forest, thorn-scrub or temperate tree.

19.s: Open stunted forests with bushes and small trees having long roots and sharp thorns repeated spines are commonly found in:
19.x: Open, stunted thorn forests with long roots and spines grow in the semi-arid rain shadow of the Deccan, i.e. western Andhra Pradesh (Rayalaseema). Eastern Odisha and the Siwalik–Terai are moist deciduous, and NE Tamil Nadu has dry evergreen forest.

19.s: Which of the following tree is valued over centuries in Rajasthan for its moisture retaining and other useful properties?
19.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
19.x: The khejri (Prosopis cineraria), Rajasthan's state tree, has long been valued for its drought tolerance, soil and moisture benefits, fodder and fuel. Ficus, pipal and neem are not the desert tree meant.

19.s: Sandalwood is commonly found in which of the following forests?
19.x: Sandalwood grows in the tropical deciduous (mainly dry deciduous) forests of south India. It is not an evergreen, alpine or mangrove species.

19.x: Khejri is a classic multipurpose social-forestry tree: fuel, fodder, green manure and soil improvement in dry areas. Eucalyptus is a fast-growing monoculture species, not the textbook multipurpose example.

19.x: Maximum plant diversity is found in the tropical evergreen forests (wet evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the Western Ghats and the NE). Moist deciduous, sub-tropical and temperate forests are less diverse.

19.s: The greatest diversity of animal and plant species occurs in:
19.x: Tropical moist (rain) forests hold the greatest variety of plant and animal species: warm, wet conditions all year support many layers of life. Temperate forests, taiga, savanna, grasslands and deserts are far less diverse.

19.s: Which one of the following ecosystems has maximum plant biomass?
19.x: Tropical rain forests have the maximum plant biomass: tall trees (45–60 m) in a dense, multi-layered canopy. Deciduous forests and desert shrubs carry much less.

19.s: "Leaf litter decomposes faster than in any other biome and as a result the soil surface is often almost bare. Apart from trees, the vegetation is largely composed of plant forms that reach up into the canopy vicariously, by climbing the trees or growing as epiphytes, rooted on the upper branches of trees." This is the most likely description of
19.x: Rapid leaf-litter decay, an almost bare soil surface, and climbers and epiphytes reaching the canopy describe the tropical rain forest. Coniferous, dry deciduous and mangrove forests do not fit.

19.x: Tropical (evergreen rain) forests grow near the equator, where it is hot and wet all year. Coniferous forests are boreal, and deciduous forests need a dry season.

18.s: Which one of the following soil types of India is rendered infertile by the presence of excess iron?
18.x: Laterite soil is left rich in iron and aluminium oxides after intense leaching, and this excess iron with poor nutrients makes it infertile. Desert, alluvial and podzolic soils are not iron-rich in this way.

18.s: Which of the following soils is most suited for tea plantation?
18.x: Tea needs slightly acidic soil without calcium and good drainage, so it is grown on hill slopes. Alkaline, alluvial and regur soils do not suit it.

18.x: Red soil covers almost all of Tamil Nadu and about 60% of Andhra Pradesh's cultivated area. Punjab–Haryana have alluvium, Rajasthan–Gujarat desert and black soil, HP–J&K mountain soils.

18.s: When you travel in certain parts of India, you will notice red soil. What is the main reason for this colour?

18.s: Which one of the following best describes forest and mountain soils?
o: Deep black soils formed from basalt in the Deccan Trap
Sandy soils rich in nitrogen and humus in western Rajasthan
Humus-rich soils on slopes, generally poor in potash and phosphorus
Salt-crusted soils of the coastal deltas

18.tq: Use the distinctive humus and nutrient combination to identify the soil.
xs: Forest and mountain soils are **humus-rich on slopes** and **poor in potash and phosphorus** — option **(3)**.
Basalt-derived = **black**; sandy desert = **arid** (and arid soil is poor in N and humus); salt crust = **saline**.
xa: They are **acidic** on upper slopes; **mountain meadow soils** occur above the tree line.

Crops: **plantations, fruit**.

18.s: Which group consists only of soils generally described as acidic?

xs: **Laterite, peaty and forest** soils are acidic — option **(2)**.
**Black** and **saline-alkaline** soils are **neutral to alkaline**, so groups with them are wrong.
xa: Peaty soils are **black, heavy and highly acidic**.

2. From the surface downward, the order of horizons is O, A, B, C, R.
3. By volume, a good soil has about 45% mineral matter, 5% organic matter, 25% water and 25% air.
4. Soil colour is one of the five factors of soil formation.
How many of the above statements are correct?
18.x: Statement 4 is wrong: the five factors are parent material, climate, relief, organisms and time; soil colour is a property, not a factor. The B horizon accumulates washed-down minerals, the order is O → A → B → C → R, and the 45/5/25/25 composition is correct. So three are correct.

18.s:
Consider the following statements:

2. India's average soil organic carbon is reported to have fallen from 1% to 0.3% in 70 years.
3. Percolation is the entry of water into the soil at the surface.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
18.x: Statement 3 is wrong: entry of water at the surface is infiltration; percolation is its movement down through the soil column. SOC binds aggregates and raises infiltration, and India's SOC reportedly fell from 1% to 0.3%. So 3 only.

28.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the order of iron content is magnetite (~70–72%) > haematite (60–70%) > limonite (40–60%) > siderite (lowest). Haematite is the most used and India's largest reserve type. So 1 and 2 only.

28.x: Statement 1 is wrong: aluminium, like K, Na, Ca and Mg, is never found free; gold, silver, platinum and copper occur native. German silver is Cu 60, Ni 20, Zn 20 (no silver), and potassium is never free. So only two are correct.

22.tq: Discriminate the Cheyyeru from the Chitravathi.
n: Chitravathi is a tributary of Penna. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 10-15]
Cheyyeru is formed by the confluence of Bahuda and Pancha. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 10-15]

xs: The incorrect statement is "**Chitravathi is formed by the confluence of Bahuda and Pancha**" — option **(2)**.
It is the **Cheyyeru** that is formed by the confluence of **Bahuda** and **Pancha**; it joins the Penna at **Gundlamada**, **Kadapa**.
The other three are correct: the **Chitravathi** is a Penna tributary from **Chikkaballapur** (Karnataka), joining at **Gandikota, Kadapa**.
xa: **Puttaparthi** lies on the **Chitravathi**.
The **Kundu (Kunderu)** joins the Penna at **Adinimmayapalli**; it is the **"Sorrow of Nandyal"**.
The **Papagni** joins near **Kamalapuram** (right bank), rising in the **Nandi Hills**.
The **Annamayya dam** is on the **Cheyyeru**.

21.s: The state of Andhra Pradesh gets its most of the rain fall during
21.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
21.x:
Most books and keys: August–September. Strictly: by IMD 1989–2018 means the three months June–August hold more rain (366 mm) than August–September (289 mm), though August (143 mm) and September (146 mm) are the two wettest single months; NextGen/Rocket name July as the rainiest month (IMD rainfall monograph 2020 p.5; NextGen AP Geography 02 p.6).
AP gets about two-thirds of its rain from the SW monsoon (mid-June–September), and by IMD state means August and September are its two wettest months, so the key is August–September. November–December (NE monsoon) matters mainly for Nellore and Rayalaseema; January–February is the dry winter.

21.s: What type of climate does Andhra Pradesh have?
21.x: Andhra Pradesh has a tropical (monsoon) climate - hot summers and rain from the south-west and north-east monsoons.

21.s:
Arrange the following seasons of Andhra Pradesh in chronological order of their usual periods, beginning with the earliest:
A. Retreating monsoon
B. Winter
C. Summer
D. South-west monsoon
21.x: Winter is January–February, summer is March to mid-June, the south-west monsoon is mid-June to September, and the retreating monsoon is October–December.
21.tq: Fix the first and last seasons, then place the monsoon transition periods.
xs: The order is **Winter → Summer → SW monsoon → Retreating monsoon (B, C, D, A)** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Winter**: **January-February**; **Summer**: **March to mid-June**.
**SW monsoon**: **mid-June to September**; **Retreating monsoon**: **October-December**.
xa: The **SW monsoon** brings about **2/3 (65-70%)** of AP's rainfall; **July** is the wettest month.
The **retreating / NE monsoon** brings about **1/3**, mainly to **Rayalaseema** and the southern coastal districts.
**Mango showers** are pre-monsoon showers in **April-May** that help mangoes ripen.

21.s: Which districts form the heat-wave belt of Andhra Pradesh?
21.x: Palnadu, Kurnool and Anantapur form the heat-wave belt, peaking in May–June.

21.x: Groundwater recovered, so the watershed works did their job; flat yields point to the community neglecting crop diversification and soil management. Excess rain or poor watershed design would not raise groundwater.

23.s: Which one of the following statements regarding problem soils is correct?
o: Alkalinity increases the availability of all plant nutrients.
Salinity can lower yields and break down soil structure.
Salinity generally improves soil structure and raises yields.
Alkalinity is caused only by excessive organic matter.
23.x: Salinity lowers crop yields and may break down soil structure. Alkalinity reduces nutrient availability and may be associated with limestone, basalt or alkaline irrigation water.
23.tq: Reject the reversed effect and identify the precise soil-problem consequence.
xs: **Salinity** lowers yields and breaks down soil structure — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Alkalinity** (high pH) **cuts** nutrient availability; it comes from **limestone/basalt** parent rock or **alkaline irrigation water**, not organic matter.
xa: Saline soils → **drain and leach** salts.
Alkaline soils → add **gypsum**.
**39 watersheds (896 villages)** are classed "saline" (2025-26).

23.s: Which of the following statements about saline and alkaline soils is incorrect?
o: Saline and alkaline soils occur in arid, semi-arid and poorly drained regions.
The largest area of saline soil is in Rajasthan.
Uttar Pradesh has the maximum alkali area.
Gujarat has the largest area of saline soil.
23.x: Option B is incorrect: Gujarat, not Rajasthan, has the largest saline area. Uttar Pradesh has the most alkali land.
n: Saline or alkaline soil occurs in arid and semi-arid regions. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Saline or alkaline soil occurs in poorly drained or irrigated regions. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Gujarat has the largest area of saline soil. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Uttar Pradesh has the maximum alkali area. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Saline or alkaline soil occurs in Gujarat. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Saline or alkaline soil occurs in Rajasthan. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Saline or alkaline soil occurs in Uttar Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
xs: The incorrect statement is "**The largest area of saline soil is in Rajasthan**" — option **(2)**.
The **largest area of saline soil** is in **Gujarat**.
**Uttar Pradesh** has the **maximum alkali area**.
Saline soils occur in **Gujarat, Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, UP** and other **irrigated or arid** regions.
xa: **Saline soil** contains **excess soluble salts**.
AP delta regions face **salinity and waterlogging** from poor drainage + faulty irrigation.
Alkaline soils are reclaimed with **gypsum**.
**39 watersheds (896 villages)** are classed "saline" in AP.

30.s: Andhra Pradesh has largest deposits of which of the following mineral?
30.x:
No printed key. Two options fit: AP has ~96% of chrysotile asbestos (IMYB 2022) and also the largest uranium resources (1,44,541 t U3O8 in a 2017 government table, web search); chrysotile is keyed as the near-monopoly.
Andhra Pradesh (Kadapa) holds about 96% of India's chrysotile asbestos resources (7.98 of 8.32 lakh t). It also leads in uranium (Tummalapalle), but not in iron ore or marble.

n: Anantapur was the first place in Andhra Pradesh for iron production. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-3]

The erstwhile Nellore district had the first-place reserves of mica in Andhra Pradesh. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-3]
Kadapa was the first place in Andhra Pradesh for asbestos production. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-3]
Kadapa had the first-place reserves of asbestos in Andhra Pradesh. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-3]
Srikakulam was the first place in Andhra Pradesh for manganese production. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-3]
Srikakulam had the first-place reserves of manganese in Andhra Pradesh. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-3]
Kurnool was the first place in Andhra Pradesh for limestone production. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-3]
Kurnool had the first-place reserves of limestone in Andhra Pradesh. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-3]
xs: The incorrect statement is "**Kadapa leads Andhra Pradesh in mica production**" — option **(3)**.
**Erstwhile Nellore** district is first in **mica** production and reserves (**Gudur** belt).
**Mangampeta** (YSR Kadapa) is AP's **barytes** deposit; Kadapa leads in **asbestos**.

30.s: From which place do diamonds in Andhra Pradesh come?
30.x: Diamonds come from Vajrakarur in Anantapur; wolframite is from Buruguwada and chromite from Kondapalli.
n: Diamonds occur at Vajrakarur in Anantapur. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 18-20]

30.x:

30.s: The Cuddapah formation of Andhra Pradesh is best described as which of the following?
o: A Cretaceous basaltic formation confined to small outliers
A Gondwana formation containing only coal deposits
A Proterozoic formation of about 1.6 billion years associated with barytes, limestone and uranium
A recent coastal formation containing only beach sands
30.x: The Cuddapah formation is Proterozoic, approximately 1.6 billion years old, and occurs mainly in the Kadapa, Nandyal, Kurnool, Annamayya and Prakasam areas. It contains barytes, limestone, uranium and other minerals.
xs: The **Cuddapah** formation is **Proterozoic, about 1.6 billion years** old, with **barytes, limestone and uranium** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It also holds asbestos, dolomite, steatite and diamonds, in Kadapa, Nandyal, Kurnool, Annamayya and Prakasam.
Cretaceous basalt outliers are the **Deccan Trap**; coal is **Gondwana**; beach sands are the **coastal sands**.
xa: The **Kadapa (Cuddapah) basin** is AP's **oldest basin** (APHQ 2019).
**Tummalapalle** uranium (YSR Kadapa) lies in the Cuddapah basin; its ore is **low-grade**.
**Mangampeta** barytes and Kadapa **steatite** (soapstone) both come from the Cuddapah system.
⚠ **Gondwana** = coal; **Cuddapah** = barytes; **khondalites** = bauxite.

1. In 2001, cultivators formed 31.7% and agricultural labourers 26.5% of workers.
2. In 2011, agricultural labourers outnumbered cultivators for the first time.
3. Agriculture's share in the workforce fell from 58.2% in 2001 to 48.9% in 2011.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
46.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: agriculture's share fell to 54.6% in 2011; about 48.9% is the NSSO primary-sector share for 2011-12.

46.s:
Consider the following statements about Census 2011:
1. India counted 4,818.89 lakh workers, of whom 24.8% were marginal workers.
2. India's Work Participation Rate was 39.8%.
3. The male and female Work Participation Rates were 53.3% and 25.5%.
4. Main workers formed about 60% of all workers.
How many of the above statements are correct?
46.x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: main workers were 75.2% of workers; about 60% of the population were non-workers.

46.s: According to Engels:
o: A woman's work is never complete
Women should be hired last and fired first
Women are in reserve labor force
Women are only marginal labor force
46.x: Engels and Marx treated women as part of the reserve army of labour, drawn in during booms and pushed out in slumps. 'Only a marginal labour force' is not Engels' phrase.

46.s: Consider the following statements: A. Households in all societies differentiate various household activities and responsibilities by gender. B. For women, production and reproduction are two interlinked activities. C. Much of the work women do, although productive, is unpaid. D. Men have always played a minor role in domestic work; societies tending to assume that they have paid work outside the home.
46.x: All four statements follow the sociology of gendered work: tasks are divided by gender, production and reproduction interlink for women, much of their work is unpaid, and men have done little domestic work.

46.s: Which of the following is identified as a reason for the rise in female work participation in India?
o: Universal availability of flexible working hours
46.x: Broader survey coverage is a stated reason for the rise, along with subsistence farming, unpaid family work, distress and return migration; flexible hours are not available universally.

46.s: Which of the following is NOT cited as a reason for low female work participation in India?
46.x: MGNREGS work raised rural female WPR; mechanisation, schooling of girls and safety are reasons for low levels.

46.s:
Consider the following statements about female labour force participation (15+) in India:
1. It rose from 23.3% in 2017-18 to 37% in 2022-23.
2. On Claudia Goldin's U-curve, India was on the falling half till 2018-19.
3. It reached about 50% in 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
46.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: female LFPR was about 40% in 2025.

46.s:
Consider the following statements about women in Indian agriculture (2011):
1. Women formed 55% of agricultural labourers.
2. Women held 24% of operational holdings.
3. Men's out-migration has led to the feminisation of farm work.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
46.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: women held only 12.8% of operational holdings; 24% is their share of cultivators.

46.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Mechanisation has contributed to low female work participation in India.
Reason (R): Mechanisation reduces the demand for manual labour, on which much of women's farm work depends.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
46.x: Both are true and R explains A: the notes list mechanisation first among the causes of low female participation.

46.s: Which of the following is NOT a Census category of non-workers?
46.x: The Census categories include students, household-duty persons, dependants, pensioners, rentiers, beggars or vagrants and others. Permanent industrial employers are not listed as a category.
46.tq: Identify the outsider in a classification list.
xs: **Permanent industrial employers** are not a non-worker category — option **(1)**.
Census non-workers: **students**, **household duties**, **dependants**, **pensioners**, **rentiers**, **beggars/vagrants**, others.
xa: Worker categories: **cultivators**, **agricultural labourers**, **household industry**, **other workers**.

46.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Cultivator — Works on another person's land for wages
Agricultural labourer — Cultivates only government land
Household industry worker — Production within the household
Other worker — Works exclusively in agriculture
46.x: A household industry worker is engaged in production within the household, such as handloom work. A cultivator works on own or leased land, while an agricultural labourer works on another person's land for wages.
46.tq: Match each occupational label with its precise defining activity.
xs: **Household industry worker — production within the household** (e.g. **handloom**) — option **(3)**.
A **cultivator** cultivates **own or leased land**; working on **another person's land for wages** = **agricultural labourer**.
**Other workers** do **non-farm** work — factory, trade, transport, services, government.
xa: Household industry = **3.8%** of India's workers (2011).
Main worker: **183+ days**; marginal: less.

46.s: In the Census, how is a person working on another's land for wages classified?
46.x: Agricultural labourers work on another's land for wages; cultivators work own or leased land.

46.s:
Match List-I (Census term) with List-II (Meaning):
List-I | List-II
a. Main worker | i. Worked less than 183 days in the reference year
b. Marginal worker | ii. Works on own or leased land
c. Cultivator | iii. Production within the household, e.g. handloom
d. Household industry worker | iv. Worked 183 days or more in the reference year
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
46.x: Main worker – 183+ days (6 months); marginal – less than 183 days; cultivator – own or leased land; household industry – production within the household.

46.s:
Consider the following statements about a Census Town:
1. It has a population of at least 5,000.
2. At least 75% of its male main workers are in non-agricultural work.
3. It has a population density of at least 300 persons per sq km.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
46.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the density criterion is 400 persons per sq km.

46.s:
Consider the following statements about Work Participation Rate (WPR):
1. WPR tends to be higher in several less-developed, hill and tribal states.
2. Subsistence activities in such regions often require greater dependence on manual labour.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
46.x: Both are correct; the greater need for manual labour in subsistence activities explains the higher WPR in these states.

46.s:
Consider the following statements about the Census 2011 Work Participation Rate of Andhra Pradesh:
1. Calculated from 230.81 lakh workers out of 495.77 lakh population, it was about 46.6%.
2. It was lower than the all-India rate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
46.x: 230.81 / 495.77 gives about 46.6%, which is higher than the all-India rate, so statement 2 is wrong.

46.s:
Match List-I with List-II (Census 2011 occupational pattern):
List-I | List-II
a. Himachal Pradesh and Nagaland | i. States with a high share of cultivators
b. Delhi, Chandigarh and Puducherry | ii. States/UTs with a high share of other workers
c. Chittoor | iii. AP district with the highest share of cultivators
d. West Godavari | iv. AP district with the highest share of agricultural labourers
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
46.x: HP and Nagaland – high cultivators; Delhi, Chandigarh, Puducherry – high other workers; in AP, Chittoor has the highest cultivators and West Godavari the highest agricultural labourers.

46.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh (Census 2011):
1. Its 230.81 lakh workers give a WPR of about 46.6%, above the national rate.
2. Cultivators formed the largest category of its workers.
3. Its 86.12 lakh main agricultural labourers were about 45% of its main workers and nearly 1 in 10 of India's.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
46.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: agricultural labourers were the largest category (47.9%); cultivators were only 14.5%.

46.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh as per PLFS 2023-24:
1. Its LFPR was 47.5%, above India's 45.1%.
2. Its WPR was 45.6%.
3. Its female LFPR (35.8%) was below India's (31.7%).
4. Higher rural female WPR is partly due to MGNREGS.
How many of the above statements are correct?
46.x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: AP's female LFPR of 35.8% is above India's 31.7%.

46.s: The one-hour Current Weekly Status rule may conceal which of the following?
o: Only long-term unemployment among urban graduates
The statutory duration of MGNREGA employment
The exact size of the organised workforce
Underemployment and inadequate utilisation of labour
46.x: The one-hour CWS criterion can classify a person as employed even when work is insufficient, thereby hiding underemployment.
46.tq: Apply the measurement concept to a short employment scenario and identify what the indicator may miss.
xs: The **1-hour CWS rule** may hide **underemployment** and **distress** — option **(4)**.
Anyone who worked **1 hour on any day** of the week counts as employed.
xa: Rising **unpaid family work** may also mask distress.
⚠ A fall in UR may reflect **distress entry** into low-productivity work.

46.s:
Match List-I (PLFS indicator) with List-II (Formula):
List-I | List-II
a. LFPR | i. Employed + unemployed
b. WPR | ii. Unemployed / labour force
c. Unemployment rate | iii. (Employed + unemployed) / population x 100
d. Labour force | iv. Employed / total population x 100
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
46.x: LFPR = (employed + unemployed) / population x 100; WPR = employed / population x 100; UR = unemployed / labour force (the labour force = employed + unemployed).

46.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Under Current Weekly Status, a person who worked one hour on any day of the reference week is counted as employed.
Reason (R): Under Usual Principal and Subsidiary Status, a person is employed if he or she worked 30 or more days in 365 days.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
46.x: Both are true, but R describes the UPSS rule and does not explain the CWS rule in A.

46.s:
Consider the following statements about the Periodic Labour Force Survey:
1. It is conducted by the National Statistical Office under MoSPI.
2. PLFS 2025 (annual) gave LFPR 59%, WPR 57% and unemployment about 3%.
3. For January-March 2026 (CWS, 15+), the unemployment rate was 3.0%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
46.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Jan-Mar 2026 CWS unemployment rate was 5.0% (LFPR 55.5%, WPR 52.8%).

46.s:
Consider the following statements about employment in Q2 FY26 (July-September 2025):
1. Agriculture accounted for 42.4% of employment.
2. Self-employment accounted for 55.8% of employment.
3. Casual labour accounted for 28.9% of employment.
4. A falling unemployment rate may reflect distress entry into low-productivity work.
How many of the above statements are correct?
46.x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: casual labour was 18.9%.

46.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: MGNREGA – Up to 100 days of wage work per rural household a year
PMEGP – Merger of PMRY and REGP
46.x: PMEGP's nodal agency is KVIC, not NABARD.
xa: ⚠ MGNREGA **Act 2005**, **launched 2006** — at **Bandlapalli (Anantapur)**, AP.
**NAPS (FY26)**: **6,100+** enterprises; **9.9 lakh** apprentices.
AP's poverty strategy cites **10 lakh+ SHGs**.

46.s:
Consider the following statements about employment programmes:
1. MGNREGA was launched on 2 February 2006 at Bandlapalli in Anantapur district.
2. The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, which replaced MGNREGA, guarantees 150 days of work.
3. PMEGP (2008), which merged PMRY and REGP, has KVIC as its nodal agency.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
46.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the VB-G RAM G Act (from 1 Jul 2026) guarantees 125 days.

46.s:
Consider the following statements about e-Shram:
1. It was launched on 26 August 2021 as a database of unorganised workers.
2. Registered workers get a 16-digit Universal Account Number.
3. About 31.89 crore workers were registered by 18 August 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
46.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the UAN has 12 digits.

51.s: Identify the correct names of the tribes living in Madhya Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Manipur and Tripura respectively.
51.x: Baigas live in MP, Gaddis in Himachal, Chirus in Manipur and Lushais in Tripura (and Mizoram). The other sets mix Sikkim, Meghalaya, Nilgiri, Andaman and Arunachal tribes.

51.s: Garo Tribes are of-
51.x: The Garo live mainly in the Garo Hills of Meghalaya (also parts of Assam and Tripura); they are matrilineal.

51.s: 'Toda' tribes mostly reside in :
51.x: The Toda live in the Nilgiri hills of Tamil Nadu (a few in adjoining Karnataka) – buffalo herders known for polyandry; not Assam, J&K or Rajasthan.

51.s: Which Tribesmen of Tamil Nadu have been employed by the State of Florida, USA to catch Pythons?
51.src: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil
51.x: Irula snake catchers of Tamil Nadu were hired by Florida (2017) to track Burmese pythons in the Everglades; they run the anti-venom cooperative and two received Padma Shri in 2023.

51.s: Which of the following tribe celebrates the Kherai puja festival?
51.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) / Technical Assistan
51.x: Kherai puja is the chief festival of the Bodo of Assam, worshipping Bathou (Bwrai). Santhal, Ao Naga and Bhil have other festivals.

51.s: Santhal tribe people live in these states
51.x: Santhals live in Jharkhand (Santhal Parganas), West Bengal and Odisha, also Bihar and Assam – eastern India, not the south or west.

51.s:
Consider the following pairs: Tribe State
1. Limboo (Limbu) Sikkim
2. Karbi Himachal Pradesh
3. Dongaria Odisha
4. Bonda Tamil Nadu
Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
51.x: Limboo–Sikkim and Dongaria Kondh–Odisha are correct; Karbi are of Assam (not HP) and Bonda of Malkangiri, Odisha (not TN) → 1 and 3 only.

51.s: Inhabitation of Tharu People is in –
51.x:
Most keys: Uttar Pradesh. Strictly: Tharus also live in Bihar (West Champaran), notified as ST there in 2003 (Down To Earth; PMF Human & Economic Geography 01 p.12).
The Tharu live in the Terai; when this was asked (1991) they were a notified ST only in Uttar Pradesh (Uttarakhand was then part of UP), so UP is the key. Arunachal and MP have no Tharus.

51.s: Which of the following is not a tribe of middle Indian region?
51.x: The Kadar are a tribe of the Anamalai hills of Kerala and Tamil Nadu, so they are not of middle India; Baiga, Muria and Kharia are central Indian tribes.

51.s: Gaddis are inhabitants of –
51.x: The Gaddi are transhumant shepherds of Himachal Pradesh (Bharmour, Chamba; Kangra) on the Dhauladhar range.

51.s: Which one of the following is not correctly matched?
51.x: Santhals belong to Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha and Bihar, so Santhals–Chhattisgarh is the wrong pair; Bhils–Gujarat, Jaunsaris–Uttaranchal and Khasis–Meghalaya are right.

51.s: Where do the Sahariya tribals, who were recently in the news, live?
51.x: The Sahariya live in Rajasthan (and MP); they were in the news for starvation deaths. Their name comes from 'sehara' (wilderness).

51.s: Which of the following is an important tribe of Dhauladhar Range ?
51.x: The Gaddi shepherds are the main tribe of the Dhauladhar range (Kangra, Chamba). Abor is Arunachal, Lepcha Sikkim, Tharu the Terai.

51.s: The 'Tamaria' tribes are found in which of the following state of India?
51.x: The Tamaria, a sub-group of the Bhumij, live in Jharkhand and were added to its ST list (as a synonym of Munda) in 2022.

51.s:
Match the following:
List I (Scheduled Tribe) a. Gaddis b. Jarawas c. Santhals d. Bhutias
List II (State/Union Territory) I. Sikkim II. Jharkhand III. Andaman and Nicobar Islands IV. Himachal Pradesh
51.x: Gaddis–Himachal (IV), Jarawas–A&N (III), Santhals–Jharkhand (II), Bhutias–Sikkim (I) → a-IV, b-III, c-II, d-I.

51.s: Santhals are inhabitant of –
51.x: Santhals live in Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha and Bihar – eastern India.

51.s: "Tharu Tribe" is residing in which of the following states of India?
51.x: The Tharu live in the Terai of Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh (also Bihar).

51.s: Which of the following tribes does not belong to North East India?
51.x: Naga, Kuki and Bodo are North-East tribes; the Khasa are a Himalayan tribe of Uttarakhand (Jaunsar-Bawar).

51.s: President Droupadi Murmu belongs to which tribal community?
51.x: President Droupadi Murmu is a member of the Santhal tribal community.
51.tq: Link the constitutional office-holder with the community explicitly associated with her.
xs: President **Droupadi Murmu** is a **Santhal** — option **(2)** is correct.
Santhals live mainly in **Jharkhand** (also West Bengal, Odisha).
xa: Santali is **Austro-Asiatic**; script **Ol Chiki**; Eighth Schedule by the **92nd Amendment, 2003**.
Santhals revere **Parasnath Hills** as **Marang Buru** (contested with Jains).
**Manjhi-Paragana** system; **Santhal Parganas**.

51.s: In which of the following do the Kadar tribe live as forest dwellers?
51.x: The Kadar live in the Anamalai hills of Kerala; the Irula live in the Nilgiris and northern Tamil Nadu.
n: The Irula tribe is located in Tamil Nadu. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Irula tribe is located in South India. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Kadar tribe is located in Kerala. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Kadar tribe is located in South India. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
xa: The **Kadar** are forest foragers of the **Anamalai** hills — the "odd one out" among middle-Indian tribes.
The **Irula** are known for **snake-venom expertise**.
**Nilgiris** tribes: **Toda, Kota, Kurumba, Irula**.
**Chenchu** live in the **Nallamala** region of AP.

51.s:
Assertion (A): The Toda and Kota tribes are associated with the Nilgiris.
Reason (R): The Muria and Maria tribes are associated with Bastar.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
51.x: Both are correct tribe–region links, but Bastar's tribes do not explain the Toda and Kota being in the Nilgiris.
xa: Changpa rear **Pashmina goats** and yaks on the **Changthang** plateau.
Other Nilgiri tribes: **Kurumba, Irula**.
**Muria** are known for the **ghotul** youth dormitory.

51.s: Which of the following about the Tharu is INCORRECT?
o: They are a pastoral tribe of the Dhauladhar Range.
They are found in the Terai of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
They are found in Nainital, Uttarakhand.
They are found in Khatima and Sitarganj of Udham Singh Nagar.
51.x: The Dhauladhar pastoralists are the Gaddi; the Tharu are a Terai people of UP, Bihar and Uttarakhand.
n: Tharu are found in the Terai of Uttar Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 29-32]
Tharu are found in the Terai of Bihar. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 29-32]
Tharu observe Diwali as a sorrow. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 29-32]
Tharu are located in Nainital, Uttarakhand. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 29-32]
Tharu are located in Khatima, Udham Singh Nagar. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 29-32]
Tharu are located in Sitarganj, Udham Singh Nagar. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 29-32]
xa: Tharu live in **joint families** and **observe Diwali as a sorrow**.
Tharu follow **Hindu religious practices**.
Gaddi: **Bharmour (Chamba)**; transhumant shepherds.

51.s: Which of the following tribe – State pairs is correctly matched?
51.x: The Lepcha live in Sikkim; the Kharwar in Uttar Pradesh, the Garo in Meghalaya and the Bodo in Assam.
n: The Kharwar tribe is located in Uttar Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Lepcha tribe is located in Sikkim. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Garo tribe is located in Meghalaya. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Bodo tribe is located in Assam. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
xa: **Khasi** (Meghalaya): matrilineal; the **youngest daughter** inherits.
**Mikir** are also in **Assam**.
**Bhutia** live in **Sikkim** with the Lepcha, Limbu, Tamang.
Tibeto-Chinese languages: **Bhotia, Lepcha, Garo, Naga**.

51.s: In which State/UT is the Bhutia tribe mainly found?
51.x: Bhutias live in Sikkim; Gaddis are of Himachal Pradesh, Santhals mainly of Jharkhand and Jarawas of the Andamans.

51.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Tribe)
a. Toda
b. Changpa
c. Dongaria Kondh
d. Onge
List-II (Habitat)
I. Niyamgiri
II. Little Andaman
III. Nilgiris
IV. Changthang
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
51.x: Toda - Nilgiris, Changpa - Changthang (Ladakh), Dongaria Kondh - Niyamgiri (Odisha), Onge - Little Andaman.

51.s:
Consider the following statements about Indian tribes:
1. The Toda of the Nilgiris are known for pukhor embroidery, which has a GI tag.
2. The name 'Bhil' is derived from 'billu' (bow); the Bhils live in the Aravalli-Vindhya-Satpura hills.
3. The Jaunsari, who combine agriculture with polyandry, live in the Jaunsar-Bawar area of Himachal Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
51.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Jaunsar-Bawar is in Dehradun district, Uttarakhand – not Himachal.

51.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Changpa of Changthang (Ladakh) have been a Scheduled Tribe since 1989.
2. The Dongaria Kondh celebrate Niyam Raja; a 2013 Supreme Court ruling helped them stop bauxite mining in Niyamgiri.
3. The Tamaria, a sub-caste of the Bhumij, were added to Jharkhand's ST list in 2019.
How many of the above statements are correct?
51.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Tamaria were added to the ST list on 8 April 2022.

51.s:
Match List-I (Tribe) with List-II (Habitat):
List-I | List-II
a. Karbi (Mikir) | i. Satpura-Melghat
b. Chenchu | ii. Karbi Anglong, Assam
c. Korku | iii. Jashpur, Chhattisgarh
d. Pahadi Korba | iv. Nallamala hills
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
51.x: Karbi (Mikir) – Assam (not Himachal); Chenchu – Nallamala (AP/Telangana); Korku – Satpura-Melghat; Pahadi Korba – Jashpur, Chhattisgarh.

51.s:
Match List-I (Tribes) with List-II (Tribal zone):
List-I | List-II
a. Chenchu, Koya, Konda Reddi | i. Central (middle India)
b. Gond, Baiga, Munda | ii. Island
c. Bhil, Mina, Warli | iii. Southern
d. Jarawa, Onge, Shompen | iv. Western
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
51.x: Chenchu, Koya, Konda Reddi (and Toda, Kota, Irula, Kadar) – Southern; Gond, Baiga, Munda – Central; Bhil, Mina, Warli – Western; Jarawa, Onge, Shompen – Island.

51.s: Among the following tribes, which one is associated with the Bhagat movement?
51.x: The Bhagat movement was the Bhil reform-and-protest movement led by Govind Guru (Govindgiri) from 1883 on the Rajasthan-Gujarat border; it ended in the Mangarh massacre of 1913. Sehariya, Bond and Meena had no Bhagat movement.

51.s: Who is using 'Duvautana' as a form of marriage for nephews (menarikam)?
51.x: Dudh-lautawa ('Duvautana') is the Gond custom of cross-cousin marriage – a sister's daughter returns to the brother's family, like the Telugu menarikam – so the Gonds of MP are right.

51.s: Which of the following tribes practice polygamy?
51.x:
Printed key: Toda only. Strictly, polygamy covers polyandry (Toda, Kota, Khasa) and polygyny (Bhil, Gond), so all five practise a form of it.
The printed key treats the Todas as the classic polygamous (polyandrous) tribe asked about.

51.s: Which of the following tribes practices polygamous marriage?
51.x:
Most keys: Toda (polyandry). Strictly: Bhils and Gonds practise polygyny, which is also polygamy (NextGen Society G2 01 p.20, 43).
The Toda are the classic example of polyandry, a form of polygamous marriage, so Toda is the expected answer; Khasis are monogamous and matrilineal.

51.s: Which one of the following scheduled tribes observe Deepawali as a sad day?
51.x: The Tharu of the Terai celebrate Hindu festivals but observe Diwali as a day of mourning; Sahariya, Baiga and Paharia do not.

51.s: In which part of India would one find "Living Root Bridges"?
51.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
51.x: Living root bridges, made by training rubber-fig roots, are found in the Khasi and Jaintia hills of Meghalaya.

51.s: Which of the following tribes is not a hunting tribe in India?
o: Irula of Tamil Nadu and Kerala
51.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
51.x: The Meena of Rajasthan are settled agriculturists, not hunters; Chenchu, Kamar and Irula are hunting and food-gathering tribes.

51.s: Which one of the Hindu festivals is celebrated as the festival of mourning by the Tharus:
51.x: Tharus observe Diwali as a festival of mourning.

51.s: Diwali is a festival of mourning among the –
51.x: Diwali is a day of mourning among the Tharus of the Terai; Khasis, Mundas and Bhils do not mourn it.

51.s: Which of the following tribes practise polyandry?

o: Mongoloids – light skin, wavy hair, narrow noses, tall stature

Negroids – dark skin, woolly hair, broad noses, thick lips
50.x: Option 1 is the incorrect description: wavy hair and a narrow nose are Caucasoid traits, while Mongoloids have straight hair, oblique eyes with an epicanthic fold and a flat face. The Caucasoid and Negroid (woolly hair, broad nose) descriptions are correct.

50.s: Which of the following explains the modern criticism of rigid racial classification?
o: Physical traits provide an objective and complete basis for classifying all populations.
All humans belong to different species based on visible traits.
Genetic studies have confirmed the permanence of colonial racial categories.
Human beings share over 99% of their genetic material and belong to one species, Homo sapiens.
50.x: Modern evidence shows that humans share over 99% of their genetic material and all belong to Homo sapiens, making rigid racial divisions scientifically subjective.
50.tq: Choose the precise scientific proposition over absolute claims about race.
xs: All humans share **over 99%** of genetic material and are **one species, Homo sapiens** — option **(4)** is correct.
So racial division is **subjective**; modern science **rejects ranking by race**.
Genetics has not confirmed colonial categories, and visible traits are not an objective basis.
xa: Old schemes rest on **visible traits** and **colonial ethnography**.
**Risley**'s race-caste theory is rejected.
**2009** genetics: most Indians descend from **ANI** + **ASI**.

Statement: Sequential cropping involves planting multiple crops in a sequence on the same field within a year, without intercrop competition. Intercropping leads to crop intensification in both time and space dimensions, with competition between crops during their growth stages. Sole cropping is the practice of growing a single crop variety on a field, not multiple varieties simultaneously. The Land Equivalent Ratio (LER) is used to measure the productivity advantage of intercropping compared to sole cropping.
Conclusion: The correct practice for measuring the productivity of intercropping in comparison to sole cropping is the use of the Land Equivalent Ratio (LER).
Which of the following can be drawn from the above statement? A) Sequential cropping and intercropping both involve growing multiple crops on the same field simultaneously. B) Sole cropping refers to growing a single crop variety, not multiple varieties. C) The Land Equivalent Ratio (LER) measures the productivity of sequential cropping. D) Intercropping has no impact on the productivity of the land.
31.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
31.x: Only B follows: sole cropping is a single variety; sequential cropping is not simultaneous, LER measures intercropping (not sequential cropping), and intercropping does affect productivity.

n: Soybean requires a warm growing season. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 80-84]

29.s:
Consider the following statements about thermal power in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Dr Narla Tata Rao TPS was AP's largest thermal station as of April 2025.
2. Sri Damodaram Sanjeevaiah TPS is at Krishnapatnam, Nellore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
29.x: Dr Narla Tata Rao TPS (2,560 MW) was AP's largest thermal station in April 2025, and Sri Damodaram Sanjeevaiah TPS (2,400 MW) is at Krishnapatnam.

29.s: The Pinnapuram project in Kurnool district is described as the world's first of which kind?
29.x: Greenko's Pinnapuram (1,680 MW pumped storage) is called the world's first integrated renewable energy storage project.

29.s:
Assertion (A): After bifurcation, Andhra Pradesh's thermal power plants bear higher coal transport costs.
Reason (R): Under the AP Reorganisation Act 2014, SCCL's equity is 51% Telangana and 49% Government of India, and AP has no share.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
29.x: Both are true and R explains A: with SCCL (Godavari valley coal) going to Telangana and the Centre (Twelfth Schedule) and AP's share nil, AP lost its coal mines and must bring coal from farther away.

29.x: Dr Narla Tata Rao TPS (2,560 MW, AP's largest) – Ibrahimpatnam near Vijayawada; Sri Damodaram Sanjeevaiah TPS – Krishnapatnam, Nellore; Rayalaseema TPS – Kalamalla, YSR Kadapa; Srisailam Right Bank (hydel) – Sunnipenta on the Krishna.

29.s:
Consider the following statements about hydel power in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The Srisailam Right Bank power house on the Krishna, begun in 1968, has 770 MW.
2. The Polavaram hydro project has 12 Kaplan units of 80 MW, i.e. 960 MW.
3. The Lower Sileru power house is at Mothugudem.
4. The Upper Sileru pumped storage project is of 1,680 MW.
How many of the above statements are correct?
29.x: Statement 4 is wrong: Upper Sileru PSP is 1,350 MW; 1,680 MW is Pinnapuram (Kurnool). Srisailam RB (Krishna, AP-Telangana border, begun 1968) is 770 MW, Polavaram is 12 x 80 = 960 MW, and Lower Sileru is at Mothugudem.

29.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh:
1. The CEA plan of August 2026 provides 7,370 MW of pumped storage and 3,931 MW of battery storage by 2035-36.
2. Phase-I of the Green Energy Corridor was finished in December 2025 with World Bank funding.
3. AP's renewable capacity was about 10,640 MW in December 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
29.x: Statement 2 is wrong: Green Energy Corridor Phase-I (finished Dec 2025) was funded by Germany's KfW. The CEA plan is 7,370 MW PSP + 3,931 MW battery (3,931 MW is battery, not pumped storage), and AP's RE was 10,639.75 MW in Dec 2025.

29.s: What is the rank of India in the Renewable Energy Country Attractive Index 2021?
29.x: India ranked 3rd in EY's Renewable Energy Country Attractiveness Index 2021.

29.s: At which of the following places is the Secretariat of the International Solar Alliance (I.S.A.) located at present?
29.x: The ISA secretariat is at Gurugram (NISE campus, Gwal Pahari, Haryana); ISA was launched by India and France at COP21, Paris 2015, but is not headquartered in Paris or New Delhi.

29.s: For which one of the following Satara is well known ?
29.x:
Official key / most books: Wind Energy Plant (Chalkewadi). Strictly, the Koyna hydro-electric project is also in Satara district, so 'Hydro-Electric Plant' is defensible (Maharashtra power-station lists).
Satara district (Maharashtra) is known for its wind farms – Chalkewadi and Vankusawade on the Sahyadri plateau; thermal and nuclear plants are not located there.

29.s: Which state has the highest potential for the development of solar energy?
29.x: By the NISE/MNRE assessment Rajasthan has the highest solar potential, about 142 GW of the national 749 GW (J&K about 111 GW next); MP, UP and Jharkhand are far lower.

29.s: Rampura, which became the first village in India to have its solar power plant, is situated in –
29.x: Rampura village in Jhansi district, Uttar Pradesh, runs on a community solar power plant (about 9 kW) set up with an NGO and is cited as India's first solar-powered village.

29.s: Which of the following states of India have the higher opportunities for the development of wind power?
29.x: Tamil Nadu and Gujarat are the leading wind States in both potential and installed capacity (Gujarat 1st, TN 2nd, Dec 2025); UP, Punjab, Bihar, Jharkhand and Odisha have low wind potential.

29.s: The biggest wind energy project in Asia with a capacity of 150 megawatts is located in :
29.x: Muppandal (Kanyakumari, Tamil Nadu) was Asia's biggest wind-farm cluster at the time (150 MW); Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka had smaller farms then.

29.s: Besides Tamil Nadu and Gujarat, which of the following is a major wind-energy State of India?
29.x: India's wind-energy States are Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh; Odisha is not among them.

29.s: Which State leads India in rooftop solar?
29.x: Gujarat leads India in rooftop solar.

2. PM Surya Ghar gives up to 200 free units of power a month through 1-3 kW rooftop systems.
3. The Green Energy Corridor is dedicated transmission to carry renewable power to the grid.
